### Create `apps/api/src/cli/custody.ts`

```ts
/**
 * The quarantine's commands (3d design, sections 6.1, 7.1, 8.10 and 10.5; section 2, rows 38 to 40), as the migrator in
 * the migrate service, around the one-shot service that moves the files, which has no database:
 *
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js quarantine-list > list
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js quarantine-record < receipt
 *
 * quarantine-list prints the plan (quarantine_plan(), executable by the migrator alone) joined to the store's naming rule
 * through the media module's quarantineNames, one line a file; it is read-only and writes no audit row. A post sealed for
 * good whose image rows are not as many as its seal recorded is left out and named on standard error, and the command
 * exits 1 after it printed every other post's lines: one bad post never stops the list for the others.
 *
 * quarantine-record takes the mover's receipt line by line in one transaction, whose last statement is the audit row
 * quarantine_recorded (counts and the receipt's digest). A well-formed line of a move the mover did is a fact about where a
 * file now is and is recorded as that, whatever the plan says now: three commands that a person runs minutes apart cannot
 * hold the database still between them. A line the plan computed before the record no longer holds is recorded all the
 * same and reported (againstPlan), and the next list moves the file back. A line that cannot be taken is reported and
 * skipped inside that transaction; no line stops the others. The command exits 1 after its commit when it reported
 * anything. A lost file raises the alert quarantine_lost to every staff account, written with the record.
 *
 * No command here moves, opens or destroys a file, and none sends anything to anyone (8.10). This file has no entry point
 * of its own, so both bundles can include it (build.mjs says why that matters).
 */
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { MEDIA_SIZES, QUARANTINE_DIRECTIONS, QUARANTINE_WORDS, type QuarantineDirection } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID } from "../auth";
import { quarantineNames, storedImageName } from "../media";
import { appendAuditRow } from "../staff";
import { Refusal, UUID, refuse, rows } from "./orders";

/** The quarantine's commands, each with its first lines of STAFF_USAGE. */
export const CUSTODY_COMMANDS = ["quarantine-list", "quarantine-record"] as const;
export type CustodyCommandName = (typeof CUSTODY_COMMANDS)[number];

export const CUSTODY_USAGE = [
  `${"  quarantine-list".padEnd(41)}print the files of sealed images to move into the quarantine, to return, to destroy or for`,
  `${"".padEnd(41)}the operator, one line a file, for the quarantine service; read-only; run it in the migrate service`,
  `${"  quarantine-record < receipt".padEnd(41)}record the quarantine service's receipt line by line, whatever the plan says now, with`,
  `${"".padEnd(41)}one audit row; run it in the migrate service (the README, Quarantine)`,
];

export type CustodyCommand = { command: CustodyCommandName };

/** Reads a custody command's words: neither takes an argument; the receipt comes on standard input. */
export function parseCustodyArgs(command: CustodyCommandName, rest: readonly string[]): CustodyCommand {
  if (rest.length > 0) throw new Error(`${command}: takes no argument${command === "quarantine-record" ? "; the receipt comes on standard input" : ""}`);
  return { command };
}

/** What a custody command answers: its lines for standard output and its notes for standard error, and whether it exits 1 after doing its work. */
export type CustodyDone = { ok: true; lines: string[]; notes: string[]; failed: boolean } | { ok: false; problem: string };

const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
const CR = String.fromCharCode(13);
const SHA256 = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;
/** A file's size as the mover prints it: a whole number of bytes over zero, in digits alone. */
const BYTES = /^[1-9][0-9]{0,15}$/;

/** The order the list prints its directions in, as quarantine_plan() names them. */
const DIRECTION_ORDER: readonly QuarantineDirection[] = QUARANTINE_DIRECTIONS;

/**
 * quarantine-list on the migrator's own connection: one read-only transaction at one snapshot, with the command line's
 * 10-second lock timeout. The lines go to standard output, as the mover reads them; the count and the posts left out to
 * standard error.
 */
async function quarantineList(tx: DbTx): Promise<{ lines: string[]; notes: string[]; failed: boolean }> {
  const { lines, mismatched } = await quarantineNames(tx);
  const sorted = [...lines].sort((a, b) => DIRECTION_ORDER.indexOf(a.direction) - DIRECTION_ORDER.indexOf(b.direction) || (a.mediaId < b.mediaId ? -1 : a.mediaId > b.mediaId ? 1 : 0));
  const out = sorted.flatMap((line) => line.files.map((file) => `${line.direction} ${line.mediaId} ${file}`));
  const count = (direction: QuarantineDirection) => sorted.filter((line) => line.direction === direction).reduce((n, line) => n + line.files.length, 0);
  const notes = [
    out.length === 0
      ? "quarantine-list: nothing is due."
      : `quarantine-list: ${count("in")} files to move in, ${count("out")} to return, ${count("destroy")} to destroy, ${count("operator")} for the operator.`,
    ...mismatched.map((post) => `quarantine-list: post ${post.postId}: its image rows do not match its seal; left out`),
  ];
  return { lines: out, notes, failed: mismatched.length > 0 };
}

/** One receipt line, as the mover prints it. */
type ReceiptLine =
  | { kind: "moved"; direction: "in" | "out"; mediaId: string; file: string; bytes: number; sha256: string }
  | { kind: "gone"; direction: "in" | "out"; mediaId: string; file: string; word: "missing" | "lost" | "refused" }
  | { kind: "destroyed"; mediaId: string; file: string; bytes: number | null; sha256: string | null }
  | { kind: "destroy_refused"; mediaId: string; file: string }
  | { kind: "have"; mediaId: string; file: string; bytes: number; sha256: string };

/** A file's name as one of its image's two under the store's naming rule, or false. */
const isFileOf = (mediaId: string, file: string) => MEDIA_SIZES.some((size) => storedImageName(mediaId, size) === file);

/** Reads one line of a receipt, or null when it is not one: malformed, or naming a file that is not one of its image's two. */
function parseReceiptLine(line: string): ReceiptLine | null {
  const f = line.split(" ");
  const [first, mediaId, file] = f;
  if (mediaId === undefined || file === undefined || !UUID.test(mediaId) || !isFileOf(mediaId, file)) return null;
  const digest = (bytes: string | undefined, sha: string | undefined) => (bytes !== undefined && sha !== undefined && BYTES.test(bytes) && SHA256.test(sha) ? { bytes: Number(bytes), sha256: sha } : null);
  if (first === QUARANTINE_WORDS.have) {
    const d = f.length === 5 ? digest(f[3], f[4]) : null;
    return d ? { kind: "have", mediaId, file, ...d } : null;
  }
  if (first === "in" || first === "out") {
    if (f.length === 4 && (f[3] === "missing" || f[3] === "lost" || f[3] === "refused")) return { kind: "gone", direction: first, mediaId, file, word: f[3] };
    const d = f.length === 6 && (f[5] === "done" || f[5] === "already") ? digest(f[3], f[4]) : null;
    return d ? { kind: "moved", direction: first, mediaId, file, ...d } : null;
  }
  if (first === "destroy") {
    if (f.length === 4 && f[3] === "already") return { kind: "destroyed", mediaId, file, bytes: null, sha256: null };
    if (f.length === 4 && f[3] === "refused") return { kind: "destroy_refused", mediaId, file };
    const d = f.length === 6 && (f[5] === "quarantine" || f[5] === "store" || f[5] === "both") ? digest(f[3], f[4]) : null;
    return d ? { kind: "destroyed", mediaId, file, ...d } : null;
  }
  return null;
}

/** A file's row of quarantine_files, as the record reads it under its lock. */
interface FileRow {
  sha256: string | null;
  returned: boolean;
  destroyed: boolean;
  lost: boolean;
}

/** What a record counted, the audit row's metadata but the receipt's digest. */
interface RecordCounts {
  in: number;
  out: number;
  destroyed: number;
  mismatched: number;
  lost: number;
  found: number;
  againstPlan: number;
  reported: number;
}

/**
 * quarantine-record on the migrator's own connection, in one transaction with the command line's 10-second lock timeout,
 * which takes quarantine_files in SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE mode first, so two records never interleave. The plan is computed
 * once, before any line is written; each line reads its file's row FOR UPDATE and writes what the line says, through the
 * table's triggers, which force every time, the post, the mark `unknown` and the stored digest. Then, for a lost file, the
 * alert quarantine_lost to every staff account, and last the audit row quarantine_recorded.
 */
async function quarantineRecord(tx: DbTx, receipt: Buffer): Promise<{ lines: string[]; notes: string[]; failed: boolean }> {
  const text = receipt.toString("utf8");
  const lines = text.split(LF).map((line) => (line.endsWith(CR) ? line.slice(0, -1) : line));
  if (lines.every((line) => line.trim() === "")) refuse("quarantine-record", "the receipt holds no line; give the quarantine service's receipt on standard input");
  await tx.execute(sql`lock table public.quarantine_files in share row exclusive mode`);
  const plan = new Set(
    (await rows<{ direction: string; media_id: string }>(tx, sql`select p.direction, p.media_id from public.quarantine_plan() p`)).map((row) => `${row.direction} ${row.media_id}`),
  );
  const counts: RecordCounts = { in: 0, out: 0, destroyed: 0, mismatched: 0, lost: 0, found: 0, againstPlan: 0, reported: 0 };
  const notes: string[] = [];
  const report = (n: number, why: string) => {
    counts.reported++;
    notes.push(`quarantine-record: line ${n}: ${why}`);
  };

  const rowOf = async (mediaId: string, file: string): Promise<FileRow | null> => {
    const [row] = await rows<FileRow & Record<string, unknown>>(
      tx,
      sql`select q.sha256, q.returned_at is not null as returned, q.destroyed_at is not null as destroyed, q.lost_at is not null as lost
            from public.quarantine_files q where q.media_id = ${mediaId}::uuid and q.file = ${file} for update`,
    );
    return row ? { sha256: row.sha256, returned: row.returned, destroyed: row.destroyed, lost: row.lost } : null;
  };
  const where = (mediaId: string, file: string) => sql`media_id = ${mediaId}::uuid and file = ${file}`;
  /** A digest that is not the one stored: reported and counted; the stored digest stays, since the files of an id never change. */
  const checkDigest = (n: number, row: FileRow | null, file: string, sha256: string | null) => {
    if (row?.sha256 && sha256 && row.sha256 !== sha256) {
      counts.mismatched++;
      report(n, `${file} has another digest than the one recorded when it was moved; the recorded digest stays`);
    }
  };
  /** A line that wrote something although the plan did not list it so: reported, and the next list moves it back. */
  const fits = (n: number, direction: string, mediaId: string) => {
    if (plan.has(`${direction} ${mediaId}`)) return;
    counts.againstPlan++;
    report(n, `image ${mediaId} no longer fits the plan; recorded where the file is, and the next list moves it back`);
  };

  for (const [index, line] of lines.entries()) {
    if (line.trim() === "") continue;
    const n = index + 1;
    const parsed = parseReceiptLine(line);
    if (parsed === null) {
      counts.reported++;
      notes.push(`quarantine-record: line ${n} is not a receipt line; skipped`);
      continue;
    }
    const { mediaId, file } = parsed;
    // Each line in a savepoint of its own: a line the database refuses is reported and leaves the others recorded.
    try {
      await tx.transaction(async (sp) => {
        const row = await rowOf(mediaId, file);
        switch (parsed.kind) {
          case "moved":
            if (parsed.direction === "in") {
              // The file is in the quarantine: a new row, a returned row moved again, or a lost row found.
              if (row === null) {
                await sp.execute(sql`insert into public.quarantine_files (media_id, file, size, sha256) values (${mediaId}::uuid, ${file}, ${parsed.bytes}, ${parsed.sha256})`);
              } else if (row.destroyed) {
                report(n, `${file} is recorded as destroyed and is in the quarantine again; nothing recorded: destroy it again by hand and note it`);
                return;
              } else if (row.returned || row.lost) {
                await sp.execute(sql`update public.quarantine_files set returned_at = null, lost_at = null, size = ${parsed.bytes}, sha256 = ${parsed.sha256} where ${where(mediaId, file)}`);
                if (row.lost) report(n, `${file} was recorded as lost and is in the quarantine; recorded where it is`);
              } else {
                checkDigest(n, row, file, parsed.sha256);
                return;
              }
              checkDigest(n, row, file, parsed.sha256);
              counts.in++;
              fits(n, "in", mediaId);
            } else {
              // The file is in the store again: its row's return.
              if (row === null) {
                report(n, `${file} has no record in the quarantine; nothing to record`);
                return;
              }
              if (row.destroyed) {
                report(n, `${file} is recorded as destroyed and is in the image store; nothing recorded: destroy it again by hand and note it`);
                return;
              }
              if (row.returned) return;
              // A row written as lost before any move takes the digest the line gives; the trigger keeps one stored before.
              await sp.execute(sql`update public.quarantine_files set lost_at = null, returned_at = now(), size = ${parsed.bytes}, sha256 = ${parsed.sha256} where ${where(mediaId, file)}`);
              if (row.lost) report(n, `${file} was recorded as lost and is in the image store; recorded as returned`);
              checkDigest(n, row, file, parsed.sha256);
              counts.out++;
              fits(n, "out", mediaId);
            }
            return;
          case "gone":
            if (parsed.word === "refused") {
              report(n, `the quarantine service refused ${file}; nothing recorded`);
              return;
            }
            if (parsed.word === "missing") {
              report(n, `${file} is missing in both places; nothing recorded (see the README, Quarantine, step 5)`);
              return;
            }
            // lost: a file found in neither place, on a run with --lost, which only a person starts.
            if (row?.destroyed) {
              report(n, `${file} is recorded as destroyed; nothing recorded`);
              return;
            }
            if (row?.lost) return;
            if (row === null) await sp.execute(sql`insert into public.quarantine_files (media_id, file, lost_at) values (${mediaId}::uuid, ${file}, now())`);
            else await sp.execute(sql`update public.quarantine_files set returned_at = null, lost_at = now() where ${where(mediaId, file)}`);
            counts.lost++;
            fits(n, parsed.direction, mediaId);
            return;
          case "destroyed":
            if (row === null) {
              report(n, `${file} has no record in the quarantine; nothing recorded`);
              return;
            }
            if (row.destroyed) return;
            if (row.lost) {
              report(n, `${file} is recorded as lost; nothing recorded`);
              return;
            }
            await sp.execute(sql`update public.quarantine_files set returned_at = null, destroyed_at = now() where ${where(mediaId, file)}`);
            checkDigest(n, row, file, parsed.sha256);
            counts.destroyed++;
            fits(n, "destroy", mediaId);
            return;
          case "destroy_refused":
            report(n, `the quarantine service refused to destroy ${file}; nothing recorded`);
            return;
          case "have":
            // The file is in the quarantine: an inventory's line. A file without a row gets its row, as a move in that
            // nobody recorded; for an image the database does not know, the trigger marks it unknown (the operator's).
            if (row === null) {
              await sp.execute(sql`insert into public.quarantine_files (media_id, file, size, sha256) values (${mediaId}::uuid, ${file}, ${parsed.bytes}, ${parsed.sha256})`);
              counts.found++;
              report(n, `${file} was found in the quarantine without a record; recorded`);
              return;
            }
            if (row.destroyed) {
              report(n, `${file} is recorded as destroyed and is in the quarantine again; nothing recorded: destroy it again by hand and note it`);
              return;
            }
            if (row.returned || row.lost) {
              await sp.execute(sql`update public.quarantine_files set returned_at = null, lost_at = null, size = ${parsed.bytes}, sha256 = ${parsed.sha256} where ${where(mediaId, file)}`);
              counts.found++;
              report(n, `${file} was recorded as ${row.returned ? "returned" : "lost"} and is in the quarantine; recorded where it is`);
            }
            checkDigest(n, row, file, parsed.sha256);
            return;
        }
      });
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof Refusal) throw err;
      report(n, `the database refused it (${(err as Error).message}); nothing recorded`);
    }
  }

  if (counts.lost > 0) {
    // quarantine_lost (W.7): to every staff account, one row for the act, with counts and its time, never a file.
    await tx.execute(
      sql`insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts) values ('quarantine_lost', 3, 'all', jsonb_build_object('count', ${counts.lost}::int, 'at', public.alert_time(now())))`,
    );
  }
  const [due] = await rows<{ due: number }>(tx, sql`select (c.due_in + c.due_out)::int as due from public.quarantine_counts() c`);
  const receiptSha256 = createHash("sha256").update(receipt).digest("hex");
  await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "quarantine_recorded", targetType: null, targetId: null, requestId: null, metadata: { ...counts, receiptSha256 } });
  return {
    lines: [
      `quarantine-record: ${counts.in} files recorded as moved, ${counts.out} as returned, ${counts.destroyed} as destroyed, ${counts.lost} as lost, ${counts.found} found without a record. Still due: ${due!.due}.`,
    ],
    notes,
    failed: counts.reported > 0,
  };
}

/** A custody command on the migrator's own connection. The receipt is read before any connection is used: nothing holds a lock while a pipe drains. */
export async function custodyCommand(migrateDb: Db, cmd: CustodyCommand, input: () => Promise<Buffer>): Promise<CustodyDone> {
  try {
    if (cmd.command === "quarantine-list") {
      const done = await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`set transaction isolation level repeatable read, read only`);
        await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
        return quarantineList(tx);
      });
      return { ok: true, ...done };
    }
    const receipt = await input();
    const done = await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
      return quarantineRecord(tx, receipt);
    });
    return { ok: true, ...done };
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof Refusal) return { ok: false, problem: err.message };
    throw err;
  }
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/quarantine.ts`

```ts
/**
 * The mover of the quarantine (3d design, sections 5 "The services", 7.1 and 8.10; section 2, rows 38 to 40): an entry
 * point of its own, dist/quarantine.js, run by the operator alone as the one-shot Compose service `quarantine`:
 *
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt
 *
 * The service's command names the two roots, `node dist/quarantine.js /media/store /media/quarantine`, and the program
 * refuses to start without both (a test passes two temporary directories the same way). It reads the list that
 * `staff.js quarantine-list` printed, one line a stored file, "<in|out|destroy|operator> <image id> <file>", and prints
 * its receipt, which `staff.js quarantine-record` takes line by line:
 *
 * - `in` and `out`: copy the file from the one root to the other under a temporary name, sync it, compare the SHA-256 of
 *   source and copy, rename the copy to its name, sync the directory, and only then unlink the source; print
 *   "<direction> <id> <file> <bytes> <sha256> done", or `already` when the file was where its direction wants it (with
 *   the same digest: only a source that is left is unlinked), `missing` when it is in neither place (`lost` on a run with
 *   --lost), or `refused` (a name outside the layout, a copy whose digest differs, a file that is not a plain file);
 * - `destroy`: take the digest first, then unlink the file in the quarantine and, when the store holds one of the same
 *   name, there too, and print where it was found: `quarantine`, `store`, `both`, or `already` when in neither;
 * - `operator`: a file the quarantine holds for an image the database does not know is left alone;
 * - with --inventory and no list: nothing moves, and one line "have <id> <file> <bytes> <sha256>" is printed for every
 *   file the quarantine holds.
 *
 * It decodes nothing and opens no file but those the list names. A crash leaves a file in one place or in both, never in
 * neither, and the next run finishes it. One bad line never stops a run: it is printed with its word, the next line is
 * taken, and the run exits 1 at its end. The directory's sync is skipped only where the platform refuses it (EPERM on
 * Windows, where only the tests run); any other error ends the run, with every file still in one place or in both.
 *
 * It opens no database and no socket, holds no credential, and imports no module of the API: the service has no network
 * and no environment and mounts the two volumes alone, so the program that moves sealed files can send them nowhere, and
 * neither the API nor the worker ever mounts the quarantine. It keeps its own copy of the store's naming rule (the media
 * module's storedImageName and handover.ts's) and of the receipt's words (the contracts' QUARANTINE_WORDS); unit tests
 * hold the copies equal.
 */
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import { constants } from "node:fs";
import { mkdir, open, readdir, rename, rm, stat, unlink, type FileHandle } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";

/** The sizes the worker stores of every image, as the contracts' MEDIA_SIZES lists them. */
const SIZES = ["small", "large"] as const;
const MEDIA_ID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;
const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
const CR = String.fromCharCode(13);

/** This program's copies of the list's directions and of the receipt's words (the contracts' QUARANTINE_DIRECTIONS and QUARANTINE_WORDS). */
export const MOVER_DIRECTIONS = ["in", "out", "destroy", "operator"] as const;
export const MOVER_WORDS = {
  move: ["done", "already", "missing", "lost", "refused"],
  destroy: ["quarantine", "store", "both", "already", "refused"],
  have: "have",
} as const;
type Direction = (typeof MOVER_DIRECTIONS)[number];

/**
 * This program's copy of the store's naming rule (the media module's storedImageName): where the worker keeps one size of
 * an image, relative to a root, with forward slashes: files/<aa>/<id>/<size>.webp. The quarantine has the same layout.
 */
export function storedName(id: string, size: (typeof SIZES)[number]): string {
  if (!MEDIA_ID.test(id)) throw new TypeError("not a media id");
  return `files/${id.slice(0, 2)}/${id}/${size}.webp`;
}

/** Whether a name is one the rule makes for this image id: anything else is outside the layout and is never opened. */
export function isStoredName(name: string, id?: string): boolean {
  const parts = name.split("/");
  if (parts.length !== 4) return false;
  const [, , named, file] = parts;
  const size = SIZES.find((s) => file === `${s}.webp`);
  if (size === undefined || !MEDIA_ID.test(named!) || storedName(named!, size) !== name) return false;
  return id === undefined || id === named;
}

/** Follows no symlink at the last path component where the platform can say so, and never waits on a FIFO. */
const READ_FLAGS = constants.O_RDONLY | (constants.O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0) | (constants.O_NONBLOCK ?? 0);

/** The bytes of a plain file, null when there is nothing under the name, or "other" for anything that is not a plain file. */
async function readPlain(file: string): Promise<Buffer | null | "other"> {
  let handle;
  try {
    handle = await open(file, READ_FLAGS);
  } catch (err) {
    const code = (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
    // Nothing there, or a part of the path that is no directory: the file is not in this place.
    if (code === "ENOENT" || code === "ENOTDIR") return null;
    return "other";
  }
  try {
    if (!(await handle.stat()).isFile()) return "other";
    return await handle.readFile();
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

const sha256 = (data: Buffer) => createHash("sha256").update(data).digest("hex");

/** What ends a run: an error the run cannot go past without leaving a file's place uncertain. */
class RunEnded extends Error {}

/**
 * Syncs a directory, so that a rename or an unlink in it survives a crash of the host. Windows refuses to sync a
 * directory (EPERM), and only the tests run there: the sync is skipped for that error alone.
 */
async function syncDirectory(dir: string): Promise<void> {
  const handle = await open(dir, constants.O_RDONLY);
  try {
    await handle.sync();
  } catch (err) {
    if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "EPERM") throw err;
  } finally {
    await handle.close();
  }
}

export interface QuarantineOptions {
  /** The image store's root and the quarantine's root, the program's two arguments. */
  store: string;
  quarantine: string;
  /** The list on standard input; ignored by an inventory. */
  input: string;
  /** --lost: a file in neither place is printed `lost` in the place of `missing`. */
  lost?: boolean;
  /** --inventory: no list is read, nothing moves, and every file the quarantine holds is printed as a `have` line. */
  inventory?: boolean;
  log: (line: string) => void;
  error: (line: string) => void;
  /** Tests: writes a copy's bytes into its new file; the handle's own write unless a test passes one that writes other bytes. */
  writeCopy?: (file: FileHandle, data: Buffer) => Promise<void>;
  /** Tests: the directory's sync, which a test makes fail with another error than the platform's refusal. */
  syncDirectory?: (dir: string) => Promise<void>;
  /** Tests: called after a copy has its name and its directory is synced, before the source is unlinked: a crash there. */
  beforeUnlink?: (file: string) => Promise<void>;
}

/** Runs one list, or one inventory, and answers its exit code: 0 when every line was carried out, 1 otherwise. */
export async function runQuarantine(options: QuarantineOptions): Promise<number> {
  const sync = options.syncDirectory ?? syncDirectory;
  const where = (root: string, file: string) => path.join(root, ...file.split("/"));
  /** Syncs a directory, or ends the run: a sync that failed for another reason than the platform's refusal is a fault of the disk. */
  const synced = async (dir: string) => {
    try {
      await sync(dir);
    } catch (err) {
      const code = (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code ?? "error";
      throw new RunEnded(`quarantine: ${dir}: the directory could not be synced (${code}); the run stops here, and every file is in one place or in both`);
    }
  };

  if (options.inventory) return inventory(options);

  let failed = false;
  const lines = options.input.split(LF).map((line) => (line.endsWith(CR) ? line.slice(0, -1) : line));
  try {
    for (const [index, line] of lines.entries()) {
      if (line.trim() === "") continue;
      const fields = line.split(" ");
      const [direction, id, file] = fields as [string, string, string];
      if (fields.length !== 3 || !(MOVER_DIRECTIONS as readonly string[]).includes(direction) || !MEDIA_ID.test(id)) {
        options.error(`quarantine: line ${index + 1} is not a line of quarantine-list; skipped`);
        failed = true;
        continue;
      }
      if ((direction as Direction) === "operator") {
        // A file of an image the database does not know: the operator decides, and writes the line's direction by hand.
        options.error(`quarantine: ${file} is an operator line; left alone (the README, Restoring)`);
        continue;
      }
      if (!isStoredName(file, id)) {
        options.error(`quarantine: skipped: ${file} is outside the layout`);
        options.log(`${direction} ${id} ${file} refused`);
        failed = true;
        continue;
      }
      if (direction === "destroy") {
        const word = await destroy(id, file);
        if (word === "refused") failed = true;
        continue;
      }
      const [from, to] = direction === "in" ? [options.store, options.quarantine] : [options.quarantine, options.store];
      const word = await move(direction, id, file, from, to);
      if (word === "missing" || word === "refused") failed = true;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    if (!(err instanceof RunEnded)) throw err;
    options.error(err.message);
    return 1;
  }
  return failed ? 1 : 0;

  /** One move in its direction; prints its line and answers its word. */
  async function move(direction: string, id: string, file: string, fromRoot: string, toRoot: string): Promise<string> {
    const source = where(fromRoot, file);
    const target = where(toRoot, file);
    const done = (word: string, data: Buffer) => {
      options.log(`${direction} ${id} ${file} ${data.length} ${sha256(data)} ${word}`);
      return word;
    };
    const bare = (word: string) => {
      options.log(`${direction} ${id} ${file} ${word}`);
      return word;
    };
    const from = await readPlain(source);
    const to = await readPlain(target);
    if (from === "other" || to === "other") {
      options.error(`quarantine: ${file}: not a plain file; nothing moved`);
      return bare("refused");
    }
    if (from === null) {
      if (to !== null) return done("already", to);
      return bare(options.lost ? "lost" : "missing");
    }
    const digest = sha256(from);
    if (to !== null) {
      // The file is where its direction wants it already: only the source that is left is unlinked.
      if (sha256(to) !== digest) {
        options.error(`quarantine: ${file}: another file of the same name is at the destination; both are kept`);
        return bare("refused");
      }
      await unlink(source);
      await synced(path.dirname(source));
      return done("already", to);
    }
    await mkdir(path.dirname(target), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    // The copy is written under a temporary name of its own, which a run cut short may have left: it is never a
    // recorded file, so it is removed before the copy is written again.
    const part = `${target}.part`;
    await rm(part, { force: true });
    const handle = await open(part, "wx", 0o600);
    try {
      await (options.writeCopy ?? ((file, data) => file.writeFile(data)))(handle, from);
      await handle.sync();
    } finally {
      await handle.close();
    }
    const copy = await readPlain(part);
    if (copy === null || copy === "other" || sha256(copy) !== digest) {
      await rm(part, { force: true });
      options.error(`quarantine: ${file}: the copy's digest differs; the copy is removed and the source kept`);
      return bare("refused");
    }
    await rename(part, target);
    await synced(path.dirname(target));
    await options.beforeUnlink?.(file);
    await unlink(source);
    await synced(path.dirname(source));
    return done("done", from);
  }

  /** One destroy line: the digest first, then the unlink in the quarantine and in the store; prints its line and answers its word. */
  async function destroy(id: string, file: string): Promise<string> {
    const inQuarantine = where(options.quarantine, file);
    const inStore = where(options.store, file);
    const kept = await readPlain(inQuarantine);
    const stored = await readPlain(inStore);
    if (kept === "other" || stored === "other") {
      options.error(`quarantine: ${file}: not a plain file; nothing destroyed`);
      options.log(`destroy ${id} ${file} refused`);
      return "refused";
    }
    const data = kept ?? stored;
    if (data === null) {
      options.log(`destroy ${id} ${file} already`);
      return "already";
    }
    // The digest is taken before any unlink, so the record proves which bytes were destroyed.
    const digest = sha256(data);
    if (kept !== null) {
      await unlink(inQuarantine);
      await synced(path.dirname(inQuarantine));
    }
    if (stored !== null) {
      await unlink(inStore);
      await synced(path.dirname(inStore));
    }
    const word = kept !== null && stored !== null ? "both" : kept !== null ? "quarantine" : "store";
    options.log(`destroy ${id} ${file} ${data.length} ${digest} ${word}`);
    return word;
  }
}

/**
 * The inventory: one `have` line for every plain file under the quarantine's files/ whose name the layout makes, in name
 * order, and nothing moved. A name the layout does not make is reported for the operator, left where it is, and makes
 * the run exit 1; a copy that a run cut short left under its temporary name is reported and left too.
 */
async function inventory(options: QuarantineOptions): Promise<number> {
  const root = path.join(options.quarantine, "files");
  let failed = false;
  const names = async (dir: string) => (await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).catch(() => [])).sort((a, b) => (a.name < b.name ? -1 : a.name > b.name ? 1 : 0));
  for (const shard of await names(root)) {
    const shardDir = path.join(root, shard.name);
    if (!shard.isDirectory() || !/^[0-9a-f]{2}$/.test(shard.name)) {
      options.error(`quarantine: files/${shard.name} is outside the layout; left where it is`);
      failed = true;
      continue;
    }
    for (const image of await names(shardDir)) {
      const imageDir = path.join(shardDir, image.name);
      if (!image.isDirectory() || !MEDIA_ID.test(image.name) || !image.name.startsWith(shard.name)) {
        options.error(`quarantine: files/${shard.name}/${image.name} is outside the layout; left where it is`);
        failed = true;
        continue;
      }
      for (const entry of await names(imageDir)) {
        const name = `files/${shard.name}/${image.name}/${entry.name}`;
        if (entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith(".webp.part")) {
          options.error(`quarantine: ${name} is a copy a run left unfinished; the next move of its file replaces it`);
          continue;
        }
        const data = entry.isFile() && isStoredName(name, image.name) ? await readPlain(path.join(imageDir, entry.name)) : "other";
        if (data === null || data === "other") {
          options.error(`quarantine: ${name} is outside the layout; left where it is`);
          failed = true;
          continue;
        }
        options.log(`${MOVER_WORDS.have} ${image.name} ${name} ${data.length} ${sha256(data)}`);
      }
    }
  }
  return failed ? 1 : 0;
}

/** The program's arguments: its two roots, then at most one of the two flags; anything else refuses to start. */
export function parseQuarantineArgs(argv: readonly string[]): { store: string; quarantine: string; lost: boolean; inventory: boolean } | { problem: string } {
  const roots = argv.filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith("--"));
  const flags = argv.filter((arg) => arg.startsWith("--"));
  if (roots.length !== 2) return { problem: "quarantine: refused: name the image store's root and the quarantine's root, in that order" };
  if (flags.some((flag) => flag !== "--lost" && flag !== "--inventory") || flags.length > 1) {
    return { problem: "quarantine: refused: the only flags are --lost and --inventory, one at a time" };
  }
  return { store: roots[0]!, quarantine: roots[1]!, lost: flags[0] === "--lost", inventory: flags[0] === "--inventory" };
}

/** Everything on standard input. */
async function readInput(): Promise<string> {
  const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
  for await (const chunk of process.stdin) chunks.push(Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk as string));
  return Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8");
}

/** The program as the service runs it: refuses to start without both roots, each an existing directory. */
export async function main(argv: readonly string[], io: { log: (line: string) => void; error: (line: string) => void; input: () => Promise<string> }): Promise<number> {
  const args = parseQuarantineArgs(argv);
  if ("problem" in args) {
    io.error(args.problem);
    return 2;
  }
  for (const root of [args.store, args.quarantine]) {
    // A volume that is not mounted is an empty directory of the image, so a root that is no directory is a typing mistake.
    if (!(await stat(root).then((s) => s.isDirectory(), () => false))) {
      io.error(`quarantine: refused: ${root} is not a directory`);
      return 2;
    }
  }
  const input = args.inventory ? "" : await io.input();
  return runQuarantine({ store: args.store, quarantine: args.quarantine, input, lost: args.lost, inventory: args.inventory, log: io.log, error: io.error });
}

const invokedDirectly = process.argv[1] !== undefined && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href;
if (invokedDirectly) {
  void main(process.argv.slice(2), { log: (line) => console.log(line), error: (line) => console.error(line), input: readInput }).then((code) => {
    process.exitCode = code;
  });
}
```

### Create `apps/app/src/components/social/ImageFault.tsx`

```tsx
import { useCallback, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Text, View } from "react-native";
import type { MediaStatusResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { IMAGE_FAULT_WORDS } from "@/lib/moderation-words";
import { social } from "@/lib/social";

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 7.1 and 9.6): why an image of the reader's own post did not load, when its status says so. The
 * post's own answer says nothing of it (PostView is unchanged), so the image's component asks GET /api/media/:id once,
 * after a failed load, and only for the reader's own image: `restoring` while its files wait in the quarantine to be
 * returned after its seal was lifted, `lost` once korbat recorded them as lost. Anything else is what a missing image
 * shows to anyone.
 */
export type ImageFault = "restoring" | "lost";

/** The fault a status answer names, or null. */
export function imageFaultOf(answer: MediaStatusResponse): ImageFault | null {
  if (answer.status !== "ready") return null;
  if (answer.lost) return "lost";
  if (answer.restoring) return "restoring";
  return null;
}

/**
 * Asks the status of an image at most once, whatever number of times its load fails, and answers the fault it names,
 * or null when it names none or the question failed: a missing image then shows as one.
 */
export function faultAsker(ask: (id: string) => Promise<MediaStatusResponse> = social.mediaStatus) {
  const asked = new Set<string>();
  return async (id: string): Promise<ImageFault | null> => {
    if (asked.has(id)) return null;
    asked.add(id);
    try {
      return imageFaultOf(await ask(id));
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  };
}

/**
 * The fault of one image of the reader's own post, and the handler for its failed load. For an image of anyone else's
 * post the handler does nothing: only an author is told why their image is missing.
 */
export function useImageFault(id: string, own: boolean): { fault: ImageFault | null; onError: (() => void) | undefined } {
  // Kept with the image it is about: the viewer steps between images with one component.
  const [found, setFound] = useState<{ id: string; fault: ImageFault } | null>(null);
  const ask = useRef(faultAsker()).current;
  const onError = useCallback(() => {
    void ask(id).then((fault) => {
      if (fault !== null) setFound({ id, fault });
    });
  }, [ask, id]);
  return { fault: found?.id === id ? found.fault : null, onError: own ? onError : undefined };
}

/** What stands in the place of the author's own image that did not load, with the words of its fault. */
export function ImageFaultView({ fault }: { fault: ImageFault }) {
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }} className="items-center justify-center bg-zinc-900 px-3 py-4">
      <Text className={`text-center text-sm leading-5 ${fault === "lost" ? "text-red-300" : "text-zinc-300"}`}>{IMAGE_FAULT_WORDS[fault]}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

	"file" text NOT NULL,
	"post_id" uuid,
	"size" bigint,
	"sha256" text,
	"moved_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
	"returned_at" timestamp with time zone,
	"destroyed_at" timestamp with time zone,

	"lost_at" timestamp with time zone,

	CONSTRAINT "quarantine_files_file" CHECK ("quarantine_files"."file" in ('files/' || left("quarantine_files"."media_id"::text, 2) || '/' || "quarantine_files"."media_id"::text || '/small.webp', 'files/' || left("quarantine_files"."media_id"::text, 2) || '/' || "quarantine_files"."media_id"::text || '/large.webp')),
	CONSTRAINT "quarantine_files_digest" CHECK (("quarantine_files"."size" is null) = ("quarantine_files"."sha256" is null) and ("quarantine_files"."size" is null or ("quarantine_files"."size" > 0 and "quarantine_files"."sha256" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')) and ("quarantine_files"."size" is not null or "quarantine_files"."lost_at" is not null)),

	CONSTRAINT "quarantine_files_release" CHECK ("quarantine_files"."release_id" is null or "quarantine_files"."destroyed_at" is not null),

);

-- Everything below is written by hand (3d design, sections 6 and 6.1). As in 0016 to 0032: every function is owned by
-- the migrator, pins its search path to public and pg_temp, names every object schema-qualified and has EXECUTE taken
-- from PUBLIC; times the database writes are now(), the transaction's start; errors carry their code as the message under
-- SQLSTATE P0001. No function here holds an interval literal: the one day of quarantine_due is F's daily threshold, the
-- contracts' QUARANTINE_RULES.dueHours, written as alert_steps() writes it for every daily kind.
--
-- 1. The grants. 0001's default privileges gave the API role every right on a new public table; quarantine_files loses
-- them all and gets none back: only the command line, as the migrator, reads and writes it (quarantine-list through
-- quarantine_plan(), quarantine-record by its statements). The API's role reaches the quarantine through the six
-- functions below that are granted to it, which answer counts, one time and booleans, never a file's name or digest.
REVOKE ALL ON "public"."quarantine_files" FROM korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 2. quarantine_files_insert: what a row says of its image is the database's, whatever the insert supplied. `unknown` is
-- true when no image row with the id exists, so the file is one the database cannot place (the plan's operator line);
-- `post_id` is the image's post then (a row imported after a restore keeps the post it names for an image the database
-- does not know). `moved_at` is the record's time, which is not before the move; a row written again after a restore
-- (imported_at set) keeps a supplied moved_at that is not after the clock. A new row has no end but `lost`, which a
-- `lost` line writes as the row's first state, at the record's time. `lost_told`: the author's notice of a lost file is
-- owed (pending) only for an image on a post, not erased and not sealed for good; else none.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_files_insert"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_post uuid;
  v_known boolean;
BEGIN
  SELECT m.post_id, true INTO v_post, v_known FROM public.post_media m WHERE m.id = NEW.media_id;
  NEW.unknown := v_known IS NULL;
  IF v_known IS NOT NULL OR NEW.imported_at IS NULL THEN
    NEW.post_id := v_post;
  END IF;
  IF NEW.imported_at IS NULL OR NEW.moved_at IS NULL OR NEW.moved_at > clock_timestamp() THEN
    NEW.moved_at := now();
  END IF;
  NEW.returned_at := NULL;
  NEW.destroyed_at := NULL;
  NEW.release_id := NULL;
  IF NEW.lost_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.lost_at := now();
    NEW.lost_told := public.quarantine_lost_told(NEW.media_id);
  ELSE
    NEW.lost_told := NULL;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_files_insert"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 3. quarantine_files_update: a row's identity, its post, its mark and the digest it was moved with never change: the
-- files of an id never change, so a later line with another digest is reported by the command and leaves the stored
-- one (a row written as lost before any move takes the digest of the move that finds its file). An end's time is the
-- record's own when the end is set, and a row that returned and is moved again keeps its row, its returned_at cleared
-- and its moved_at the new record's time. A time already set is left as the update gives it: only the migrator writes
-- this table, and that is how a test moves a record back in time (ageCustodyForTest). `lost_told` is forced when lost_at
-- is set, and afterwards changes only from pending, through lost_told().
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_files_update"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.media_id := OLD.media_id;
  NEW.file := OLD.file;
  NEW.post_id := OLD.post_id;
  NEW.unknown := OLD.unknown;
  NEW.imported_at := OLD.imported_at;
  IF OLD.sha256 IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.size := OLD.size;
    NEW.sha256 := OLD.sha256;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.returned_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.returned_at IS NULL THEN
    NEW.moved_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF OLD.returned_at IS NULL AND NEW.returned_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.returned_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF OLD.destroyed_at IS NULL AND NEW.destroyed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.destroyed_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF NEW.lost_at IS NULL THEN
    NEW.lost_told := NULL;
  ELSIF OLD.lost_at IS NULL THEN
    NEW.lost_at := now();
    NEW.lost_told := public.quarantine_lost_told(NEW.media_id);
  ELSIF OLD.lost_told <> 'pending' OR NEW.lost_told IS NULL THEN
    NEW.lost_told := OLD.lost_told;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_files_update"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 4. Two helpers of the functions below, callable by nobody but their owner. quarantine_sealed_for_good: a seal_media in
-- force lists the post and its decision is not interim (measures_in_force; a seal taken while deciding, a person's or a
-- program's, is meant to end within hours and leaves its files in the store: section 2, row 38). quarantine_lost_told:
-- the state a lost file's notice is born in, pending only for an image of a post its author still has, not erased and
-- not sealed for good.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_sealed_for_good"(post uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.seal_posts s JOIN public.measures_in_force f ON f.id = s.action_id
                  WHERE s.post_id = quarantine_sealed_for_good.post AND f.kind = 'seal_media' AND f.decision_kind <> 'interim')
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_sealed_for_good"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_lost_told"(media uuid) RETURNS "public"."delivery_state"
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.post_media m JOIN public.posts p ON p.id = m.post_id
                            WHERE m.id = quarantine_lost_told.media AND m.erased_at IS NULL AND p.erased_at IS NULL
                              AND p.state <> 'deleted_by_author' AND NOT public.quarantine_sealed_for_good(m.post_id))
              THEN 'pending'::public.delivery_state ELSE 'none'::public.delivery_state END
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_lost_told"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "quarantine_files_insert" BEFORE INSERT ON "public"."quarantine_files" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_files_insert"();--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "quarantine_files_update" BEFORE UPDATE ON "public"."quarantine_files" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_files_update"();--> statement-breakpoint

-- 5. quarantine_plan(): what the mover is to do, one row an image (section 6.1), for staff.js quarantine-list alone, as the
-- migrator: EXECUTE to nobody. A file "has no end" while its returned_at, destroyed_at and lost_at are null. An image is
-- "in the quarantine" when each of its two files has a row with returned_at and destroyed_at null: a lost file counts
-- here, since nothing of it is left to move.
--   in:       every image row, not erased, of a post sealed for good, that is not in the quarantine;
--   out:      every image with a file without an end, not marked unknown, whose image row exists, is on a post, is not
--             erased and is not sealed for good (an unseal_media, or a stale list's move of a file whose seal was lifted);
--   destroy:  every image with a file without an end, not marked unknown, whose image row no longer exists;
--   operator: every image with a file without an end marked unknown, which nothing destroys or returns on a list's word.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_plan"() RETURNS TABLE (direction text, media_id uuid)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  WITH good AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT s.post_id FROM public.seal_posts s JOIN public.measures_in_force f ON f.id = s.action_id
     WHERE f.kind = 'seal_media' AND f.decision_kind <> 'interim'
  ), open_files AS (
    SELECT q.media_id, bool_or(q.unknown) AS unknown FROM public.quarantine_files q
     WHERE q.returned_at IS NULL AND q.destroyed_at IS NULL AND q.lost_at IS NULL GROUP BY q.media_id
  ), kept AS (
    SELECT q.media_id FROM public.quarantine_files q
     WHERE q.returned_at IS NULL AND q.destroyed_at IS NULL GROUP BY q.media_id HAVING count(*) = 2
  )
  SELECT 'in'::text, m.id FROM public.post_media m JOIN good g ON g.post_id = m.post_id
   WHERE m.erased_at IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM kept k WHERE k.media_id = m.id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'out'::text, o.media_id FROM open_files o JOIN public.post_media m ON m.id = o.media_id
   WHERE NOT o.unknown AND m.post_id IS NOT NULL AND m.erased_at IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM good g WHERE g.post_id = m.post_id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'destroy'::text, o.media_id FROM open_files o
   WHERE NOT o.unknown AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.post_media m WHERE m.id = o.media_id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'operator'::text, o.media_id FROM open_files o WHERE o.unknown
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_plan"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 6. quarantine_counts(): the sizes of the three sets the mover carries out, in images, and the earliest time a move in
-- or out became due: for `in` its seal's decided_at (the oldest seal for good in force listing the post), for `out` the
-- created_at of the newest ledger row that reversed a seal for good listing its post, or the move's own record when a
-- stale list moved the file after that. What the console's home and quarantine_due learn: counts and one time, no id.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_counts"() RETURNS TABLE (due_in integer, due_out integer, undestroyed integer, oldest timestamptz)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  WITH plan AS (
    SELECT p.direction, p.media_id FROM public.quarantine_plan() p
  ), in_at AS (
    SELECT min(f_d.decided_at) AS at
      FROM plan p JOIN public.post_media m ON m.id = p.media_id
      JOIN LATERAL (SELECT min(d.decided_at) AS decided_at FROM public.seal_posts s
                      JOIN public.measures_in_force f ON f.id = s.action_id AND f.kind = 'seal_media' AND f.decision_kind <> 'interim'
                      JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = f.decision_id
                     WHERE s.post_id = m.post_id) f_d ON true
     WHERE p.direction = 'in'
  ), out_at AS (
    SELECT min(greatest(
             (SELECT max(r.created_at) FROM public.seal_posts s
                JOIN public.decision_actions a ON a.id = s.action_id AND a.kind = 'seal_media'
                JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = a.decision_id AND d.kind <> 'interim'
                JOIN public.decision_actions r ON r.reverses_action_id = a.id
               WHERE s.post_id = m.post_id),
             (SELECT max(q.moved_at) FROM public.quarantine_files q
               WHERE q.media_id = p.media_id AND q.returned_at IS NULL AND q.destroyed_at IS NULL AND q.lost_at IS NULL))) AS at
      FROM plan p JOIN public.post_media m ON m.id = p.media_id
     WHERE p.direction = 'out'
  )
  SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM plan WHERE direction = 'in')::integer,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM plan WHERE direction = 'out')::integer,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM plan WHERE direction = 'destroy')::integer,
         least((SELECT at FROM in_at), (SELECT at FROM out_at))
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_counts"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_counts"() TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 7. seal_custody(action): the same for one seal, which its case shows (CaseDecision.custody), for the posts its ledger row
-- lists in seal_posts: `files`, two for each image row of those posts that is not erased; `moved`, how many of those
-- files have a row without an end, and `moved_at` the newest of their records; `to_return`, the files without an end of
-- the images of those posts that the plan lists under out; `files_left`, 0 until the release (Task 2) adds its released
-- files; `lost`, the files recorded as lost whose row names one of those posts. Counts and one time, never a name.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."seal_custody"(action uuid) RETURNS TABLE (files integer, moved integer, moved_at timestamptz, to_return integer, files_left integer, lost integer)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  WITH posts AS (
    SELECT s.post_id FROM public.seal_posts s WHERE s.action_id = seal_custody.action
  ), images AS (
    SELECT m.id FROM public.post_media m JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = m.post_id WHERE m.erased_at IS NULL
  ), present AS (
    SELECT q.moved_at FROM public.quarantine_files q JOIN images i ON i.id = q.media_id
     WHERE q.returned_at IS NULL AND q.destroyed_at IS NULL AND q.lost_at IS NULL
  ), to_return AS (
    SELECT p.media_id FROM public.quarantine_plan() p JOIN public.post_media m ON m.id = p.media_id JOIN posts x ON x.post_id = m.post_id
     WHERE p.direction = 'out'
  )
  SELECT (2 * (SELECT count(*) FROM images))::integer,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM present)::integer,
         (SELECT max(present.moved_at) FROM present),
         (SELECT count(*) FROM public.quarantine_files q JOIN to_return t ON t.media_id = q.media_id
           WHERE q.returned_at IS NULL AND q.destroyed_at IS NULL AND q.lost_at IS NULL)::integer,
         0,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM public.quarantine_files q JOIN posts p ON p.post_id = q.post_id WHERE q.lost_at IS NOT NULL)::integer
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."seal_custody"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."seal_custody"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 8. media_quarantined(media) and media_lost(media): whether a file of the image has a row without an end, and whether
-- one is recorded as lost. serve and the owner's status ask them only for a visible image whose file is missing, to
-- answer "being restored" or that korbat lost it, in the place of an error (section 2, row 39).
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."media_quarantined"(media uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.quarantine_files q
                  WHERE q.media_id = media_quarantined.media AND q.returned_at IS NULL AND q.destroyed_at IS NULL AND q.lost_at IS NULL)
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."media_quarantined"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."media_quarantined"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."media_lost"(media uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.quarantine_files q WHERE q.media_id = media_lost.media AND q.lost_at IS NOT NULL)
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."media_lost"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."media_lost"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 9. lost_untold(n) and lost_told(media, outcome): the dispatch job's one way to learn of a lost file whose author is owed
-- the notice (one row an image, the earliest lost first), and to record the mail's outcome, which changes a row only
-- from pending: the table is closed to the API's role.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."lost_untold"(n integer) RETURNS TABLE (media_id uuid, lost_at timestamptz)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT q.media_id, min(q.lost_at) FROM public.quarantine_files q
   WHERE q.lost_told = 'pending' GROUP BY q.media_id ORDER BY 2, 1 LIMIT greatest(lost_untold.n, 0)
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."lost_untold"(integer) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."lost_untold"(integer) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."lost_told"(media uuid, outcome "public"."delivery_state") RETURNS void
LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  UPDATE public.quarantine_files q SET lost_told = lost_told.outcome WHERE q.media_id = lost_told.media AND q.lost_told = 'pending'
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."lost_told"(uuid, "public"."delivery_state") FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."lost_told"(uuid, "public"."delivery_state") TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 10. alert_steps(), replaced from its text in 0031_recovery with section 6.1's row marked 0030: quarantine_due.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."alert_steps"() RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_now timestamptz := now();
  r record;
  v_rows integer;
  v_written integer := 0;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO r FROM public.order_rules();

  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts, message_id)
  SELECT 'contact_mail_escalated', 5, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'contact_mail_escalated' AND o.message_id = m.id AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('receivedAt', public.alert_time(m.received_at), 'dueAt', public.alert_time(m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.hour_minutes))),
         m.id
    FROM public.contact_messages m
   WHERE NOT m.stale AND m.disposition IS NULL
     AND m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.escalate_minutes) <= v_now
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auth.staff_sessions s WHERE s.created_at >= m.received_at OR s.last_used_at >= m.received_at)
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'contact_mail_escalated' AND o.message_id = m.id AND o.order_id IS NULL
                        AND o.created_at >= m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.escalate_minutes))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts, message_id)
  SELECT 'order_due', 5, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'order_due' AND o.message_id = m.id AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         -- The minutes left, rounded up and never below 0: an hour of order_rules() is hour_minutes minutes.
         jsonb_build_object('dueAt', public.alert_time(d.due_at),
                            'minutesLeft', greatest(0, ceil(extract(epoch FROM d.due_at - v_now) / extract(epoch FROM make_interval(mins => r.hour_minutes)) * r.hour_minutes))::integer),
         m.id
    FROM public.contact_messages m
   CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
     SELECT m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.hour_minutes) AS due_at,
            CASE WHEN m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.hour_minutes) <= v_now THEN m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.hour_minutes)
                 WHEN m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.remind_minutes) <= v_now THEN m.received_at + make_interval(mins => r.remind_minutes)
            END AS threshold) d
   WHERE NOT m.stale AND m.disposition IS NULL AND d.threshold IS NOT NULL
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'order_due' AND o.message_id = m.id AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= d.threshold)
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts)
  SELECT 'alert_test', 3, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'alert_test' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('at', public.alert_time(v_now))
   WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'alert_test' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= v_now - make_interval(days => 1))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- 0027 (3f design, section 6.1, the rows marked 0025): an order's steps. Its clock started again by a restart rings the
  -- phone on call again, as a message's first push, once a restart: the threshold is the restart's clock_start, so a
  -- second restart alerts again with the next free step.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts, order_id)
  SELECT 'contact_mail', 5, 'on_call',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'contact_mail' AND o.order_id = c.order_id AND o.message_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('dueAt', public.alert_time(c.deadline_at)),
         c.order_id
    FROM public.legal_order_clock c
    JOIN public.legal_orders lo ON lo.id = c.order_id
   WHERE lo.closed_at IS NULL AND NOT c.stopped AND c.clock_start IS NOT NULL AND c.items_open > 0
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.legal_order_events e WHERE e.order_id = c.order_id AND e.kind IN ('grounds_ceased', 'clarification_received'))
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'contact_mail' AND o.order_id = c.order_id AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= c.clock_start)
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- order_due for an order: a removal order that is not closed, whose clock runs, with an item neither disabled nor
  -- closed (one given effect in part is still due), at clock_start + remind_minutes and at the deadline, the later of the
  -- two that has passed. Its reminders end when it is given effect in full, closed, or stopped by an Annex III.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts, order_id)
  SELECT 'order_due', 5, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'order_due' AND o.order_id = c.order_id AND o.message_id IS NULL), 0),
         -- The minutes left, rounded up and never below 0: an hour of order_rules() is hour_minutes minutes.
         jsonb_build_object('dueAt', public.alert_time(c.deadline_at),
                            'minutesLeft', greatest(0, ceil(extract(epoch FROM c.deadline_at - v_now) / extract(epoch FROM make_interval(mins => r.hour_minutes)) * r.hour_minutes))::integer,
                            'itemsOpen', c.items_open),
         c.order_id
    FROM public.legal_order_clock c
    JOIN public.legal_orders lo ON lo.id = c.order_id
   CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
     SELECT CASE WHEN c.deadline_at <= v_now THEN c.deadline_at
                 WHEN c.clock_start + make_interval(mins => r.remind_minutes) <= v_now THEN c.clock_start + make_interval(mins => r.remind_minutes)
            END AS threshold) d
   WHERE lo.closed_at IS NULL AND NOT c.stopped AND c.clock_start IS NOT NULL AND c.items_open > 0 AND d.threshold IS NOT NULL
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'order_due' AND o.order_id = c.order_id AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= d.threshold)
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- order_unverified, daily: among the orders that are not closed and are given effect, one count for each of its three
  -- conditions: an item disabled while the order is not verified, or added after its verification; no reasons of the
  -- authority recorded; a DSA order holding a notice with no recorded end. oldestAt is the first disabling among them.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts)
  SELECT 'order_unverified', 5, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'order_unverified' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('count', u.unverified, 'textsMissing', u.texts_missing, 'holdsOpen', u.holds_open, 'oldestAt', public.alert_time(u.oldest_at))
    FROM (SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE q.unverified))::integer AS unverified,
                 (count(*) FILTER (WHERE q.texts_missing))::integer AS texts_missing,
                 (count(*) FILTER (WHERE q.hold_open))::integer AS holds_open,
                 min(q.first_effect) FILTER (WHERE q.unverified OR q.texts_missing OR q.hold_open) AS oldest_at
            FROM (SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.legal_order_items i
                                  WHERE i.order_id = lo.id AND i.disabled_at IS NOT NULL AND (lo.verified_at IS NULL OR i.added_at > lo.verified_at)) AS unverified,
                         lo.reasons IS NULL AS texts_missing,
                         (public.order_hold_until(lo.id) = 'infinity'::timestamptz
                          AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.legal_order_items i JOIN public.decisions d ON d.order_item_id = i.id
                                       WHERE i.order_id = lo.id AND d.informed_at IS NULL)) AS hold_open,
                         (SELECT min(i.disabled_at) FROM public.legal_order_items i WHERE i.order_id = lo.id) AS first_effect
                    FROM public.legal_orders lo
                   WHERE lo.closed_at IS NULL
                     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.legal_order_items i WHERE i.order_id = lo.id AND i.disabled_at IS NOT NULL)) q) u
   WHERE u.unverified + u.texts_missing + u.holds_open > 0
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'order_unverified' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= v_now - make_interval(days => 1))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- 0028 (3f design, section 6.1, the row marked 0026): hold_ending, daily, while an order has an untold decision whose
  -- order_hold_until is less than hold_warning_days ahead, so that whoever has the server checks the mailbox for an
  -- extension before the database releases. Facts: how many held notices, and the first end. A hold with no end
  -- ('infinity') is order_unverified's.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts)
  SELECT 'hold_ending', 3, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'hold_ending' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('count', h.held, 'at', public.alert_time(h.first_end))
    FROM (SELECT count(*)::integer AS held, min(u.until) AS first_end
            FROM (SELECT public.order_hold_until(i.order_id) AS until
                    FROM public.decisions d JOIN public.legal_order_items i ON i.id = d.order_item_id
                   WHERE d.kind = 'order' AND d.informed_at IS NULL) u
           WHERE u.until IS NOT NULL AND u.until < 'infinity'::timestamptz AND u.until < v_now + make_interval(days => r.hold_warning_days)) h
   WHERE h.held > 0
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'hold_ending' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= v_now - make_interval(days => 1))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- 0030 (3f design, section 6.1, the rows marked 0028): report_owed, daily, while at least one notification record is
  -- owed and was opened more than report_alert_hours ago; facts: how many, and the oldest's opening. Counts, no case.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts)
  SELECT 'report_owed', 5, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'report_owed' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('count', q.owed, 'oldestAt', public.alert_time(q.oldest_at))
    FROM (SELECT count(*)::integer AS owed, min(n.opened_at) AS oldest_at
            FROM public.authority_notifications n
           WHERE n.state = 'owed' AND n.opened_at < v_now - make_interval(hours => r.report_alert_hours)) q
   WHERE q.owed > 0
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'report_owed' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= v_now - make_interval(days => 1))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- handover_undestroyed, daily, while a production holds files, was delivered more than handover_alert_days ago and has
  -- no destroyed_at; facts: how many.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts)
  SELECT 'handover_undestroyed', 3, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'handover_undestroyed' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('count', q.undestroyed)
    FROM (SELECT count(*)::integer AS undestroyed
            FROM public.productions p
           WHERE p.files IS NOT NULL AND p.destroyed_at IS NULL AND p.delivered_at < v_now - make_interval(days => r.handover_alert_days)) q
   WHERE q.undestroyed > 0
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'handover_undestroyed' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= v_now - make_interval(days => 1))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- 0031 (3f design, section 6.1, the row marked 0029): copy_overdue, daily, while the newest copy mark is older than
  -- copy_overdue_hours, or there is none and the audit log's first row is that old; facts: the hours since the newest
  -- mark, or since that first row. This function is its one writer: no round of the API raises it as well.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts)
  SELECT 'copy_overdue', 3, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'copy_overdue' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('hours', floor(extract(epoch FROM v_now - q.since) / extract(epoch FROM make_interval(hours => 1)))::integer)
    FROM (SELECT coalesce((SELECT m.at FROM public.copy_marks m ORDER BY m.at DESC, m.id DESC LIMIT 1),
                          (SELECT l.created_at FROM public.audit_log l ORDER BY l.chain_seq LIMIT 1)) AS since) q
   WHERE q.since IS NOT NULL AND q.since < v_now - make_interval(hours => r.copy_overdue_hours)
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'copy_overdue' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= v_now - make_interval(days => 1))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  -- 0033 (3d design, section 6.1, the row marked 0030): quarantine_due, daily, while a move into the quarantine or back to
  -- the image store has been due for longer than the daily threshold (the contracts' QUARANTINE_RULES.dueHours); facts:
  -- how many images are due in and out together, and since when the oldest is. Counts and one time, no image.
  INSERT INTO public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, step, facts)
  SELECT 'quarantine_due', 3, 'all',
         coalesce((SELECT max(o.step) + 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                    WHERE o.kind = 'quarantine_due' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL), 0),
         jsonb_build_object('count', c.due_in + c.due_out, 'oldestAt', public.alert_time(c.oldest))
    FROM public.quarantine_counts() c
   WHERE c.due_in + c.due_out > 0 AND c.oldest IS NOT NULL AND c.oldest <= v_now - make_interval(days => 1)
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.alert_outbox o
                      WHERE o.kind = 'quarantine_due' AND o.message_id IS NULL AND o.order_id IS NULL AND o.created_at >= v_now - make_interval(days => 1))
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_written := v_written + v_rows;

  RETURN v_written;
END $$;

      "policies": {
        "decisions_api_all": {
          "name": "decisions_api_all",
          "as": "PERMISSIVE",
          "for": "ALL",
          "to": [
            "korbat_api"
          ],
          "using": "true",
          "withCheck": "true"
        }
      },
      "checkConstraints": {
        "decisions_rule_id": {
          "name": "decisions_rule_id",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "decisions_category": {
          "name": "decisions_category",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "decisions_category_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT')"
        },
        "decisions_automated_decision": {
          "name": "decisions_automated_decision",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" in ('fully', 'partially', 'not_automated')"
        },
        "decisions_territorial_scope": {
          "name": "decisions_territorial_scope",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"territorial_scope\" = 'worldwide'"
        },
        "decisions_review_target": {
          "name": "decisions_review_target",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"kind\" in ('review', 'correction')) = (\"decisions\".\"reviews_decision_id\" is not null) and (\"decisions\".\"kind\" = 'review') = (\"decisions\".\"appeal_id\" is not null)"
        },
        "decisions_interim": {
          "name": "decisions_interim",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" <> 'interim' or \"decisions\".\"through_seq\" = 0"
        },
        "decisions_ground_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'incompatible' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is not null"
        },
        "decisions_ground_law": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_law",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_restricted": {
          "name": "decisions_restricted",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"outcome\" <> 'restricted' or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is not null) or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_informed": {
          "name": "decisions_informed",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"informed_at\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"author_mail\"::text = 'none'"
        },
        "decisions_digests": {
          "name": "decisions_digests",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')"
        },
        "decisions_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null or \"decisions\".\"ground\" is not distinct from 'illegal'"
        },
        "decisions_law_no_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_law_no_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null"
        },
        "decisions_reversal_plain": {
          "name": "decisions_reversal_plain",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" not in ('review', 'correction') or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is null and \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null and \"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null and \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },
