```ts
  const found = await rows<{ at: string; handle: string; case_id: string; total: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select ${iso("t.created_at")} as at, p.handle, t.case_id, (count(*) over ())::int as total
          from staff_texts t join profiles p on p.id = t.author_id
         where t.kind = 'seal_declined' and t.created_at >= now() - interval '30 days'
         order by t.created_at desc, t.id desc limit ${max}::int`,
  );
  return { total: found[0]?.total ?? 0, items: found.map((row) => ({ at: row.at, handle: row.handle, caseId: row.case_id })) };
}

/** The seals taken while deciding that are in force, by the view's one definition, newest first: who took each, on which case, and what its list covers. */
export async function interimSealsInForce(q: Runner, max: number): Promise<{ total: number; items: { at: string; handle: string; caseId: string; posts: number; images: number }[] }> {
  const found = await rows<{ at: string; handle: string; case_id: string; posts: number; images: number; total: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select ${iso("d.decided_at")} as at, p.handle, m.case_id, (count(*) over ())::int as total,
               (select count(*)::int from seal_posts s where s.action_id = m.id) as posts,
               (select coalesce(sum(s.images), 0)::int from seal_posts s where s.action_id = m.id) as images
          from measures_in_force m join decisions d on d.id = m.decision_id join profiles p on p.id = d.decided_by
         where m.kind = 'seal_media' and m.decision_kind = 'interim'
         order by d.decided_at desc, m.id desc limit ${max}::int`,
  );
  return { total: found[0]?.total ?? 0, items: found.map((row) => ({ at: row.at, handle: row.handle, caseId: row.case_id, posts: row.posts, images: row.images })) };
}

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 8.2 and 10.3): the quarantine's counts for the home screen, the four values of
 * quarantine_counts() and nothing else: the API's role reaches the quarantine through such functions alone.
 */
export async function quarantineCounts(q: Runner): Promise<{ dueIn: number; dueOut: number; undestroyed: number; oldest: string | null }> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ due_in: number; due_out: number; undestroyed: number; oldest: string | null }>(
    q,
    sql`select c.due_in, c.due_out, c.undestroyed, ${iso("c.oldest")} as oldest from public.quarantine_counts() c`,
  );
  return { dueIn: row!.due_in, dueOut: row!.due_out, undestroyed: row!.undestroyed, oldest: row!.oldest };
}

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 8.4 and 10.3): where the files of each of these seals are, by seal_custody(action), keyed by
 * the seal's ledger row: counts and one time, never a file's name or digest.
 */
export async function sealCustody(q: Runner, actionIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, { files: number; moved: number; movedAt: string | null; toReturn: number; filesLeft: number; lost: number }>> {
  const custody = new Map<string, { files: number; moved: number; movedAt: string | null; toReturn: number; filesLeft: number; lost: number }>();
  for (const actionId of actionIds) {
    const [row] = await rows<{ files: number; moved: number; moved_at: string | null; to_return: number; files_left: number; lost: number }>(
      q,
      sql`select c.files, c.moved, ${iso("c.moved_at")} as moved_at, c.to_return, c.files_left, c.lost from public.seal_custody(${actionId}::uuid) c`,
    );
    custody.set(actionId, { files: row!.files, moved: row!.moved, movedAt: row!.moved_at, toReturn: row!.to_return, filesLeft: row!.files_left, lost: row!.lost });
  }
  return custody;
}

/** What became of a mail korbat owed: the delivery states a send can end in. */
export type MailState = "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "failed";

/**
 * Records what became of a decision's statement mail, only while it is still pending, so a late answer never overwrites
 * one already recorded. True when this call recorded it.
 */
/**
 * How long a transaction that records a mail's result waits for the row it records it on. Such a transaction holds the
 * row while the relay takes the mail (at most the mailer's 30 seconds), so a second sender of the same mail waits here,
 * and then finds it recorded.
 */
export const MAIL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000;

/**
 * The start of a transaction that will send a mail and record its result on a row (3c design, section 7.8, as the review
 * of the built code corrected it): the wait for a lock is bounded, and the rows are then taken with one of the three
 * functions below, before anything is sent. Taking a row for update is a write: a database that answers reads and cannot
 * write (a server in recovery, a full disk, default_transaction_read_only) refuses it, so a mail whose result could not
 * be recorded is never sent, however often it is tried. The result is recorded in the same transaction.
 */
export async function beginMailRecord(tx: DbTx): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${MAIL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
}

/**
 * Whether a later decision lifted the decision's suspension or termination, or a reversal broke its basis (3e's review,
 * proofs1): its statement, still owed, is then never sent. A statement of its own, read after the decision's row is held.
 */
export async function standingWithdrawn(tx: DbTx, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ withdrawn: boolean }>(
    tx,
    sql`select exists (select 1 from decision_actions a
                        where a.decision_id = ${decisionId}::uuid and a.kind::text in ('suspend', 'terminate')
                          and (exists (select 1 from decision_actions r where r.reverses_action_id = a.id) or public.standing_basis_broken_at(a.id) is not null)) as withdrawn`,
  );
  return row?.withdrawn === true;
}

/** Takes a decision's row while its statement's mail is still owed; false, and nothing is taken, when it is not. */
export async function lockPendingAuthorMail(tx: DbTx, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from decisions where id = ${decisionId}::uuid and author_mail = 'pending' for no key update`)).length > 0;
}

/** Takes a notice's row while its receipt is still owed (pending, or, with `folded`, folded into an update); false when it is not. */
export async function lockPendingReceipt(tx: DbTx, intakeId: string, folded = false): Promise<boolean> {
  const states = folded ? sql`receipt in ('pending', 'folded')` : sql`receipt = 'pending'`;
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from intakes where id = ${intakeId}::uuid and ${states} for no key update`)).length > 0;
}

/** Takes, in one id order, the rows of these items whose outcome mail is still owed, and answers their ids. */
export async function lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx: DbTx, itemIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
  if (itemIds.length === 0) return new Set();
  const locked = await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from intake_items where id = any(${uuids(itemIds)}) and outcome_mail = 'pending' order by id for no key update`);
  return new Set(locked.map((row) => row.id));
}

export async function recordAuthorMail(q: Runner, decisionId: string, state: MailState): Promise<boolean> {
  const updated = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`update decisions set author_mail = ${state}::delivery_state, author_mail_at = case when ${state}::text = 'sent' then now() else author_mail_at end
         where id = ${decisionId}::uuid and author_mail = 'pending' returning id`,
  );
  return updated.length > 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the dispatch job

/** A time as a timestamptz parameter. */
const at = (time: Date) => sql`${time.toISOString()}::timestamptz`;

/** The notices whose receipt is still pending and that were received before `before`, oldest first, at most `limit`. */
export async function pendingReceipts(q: Runner, before: Date, limit: number): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select id from intakes where receipt = 'pending' and received_at < ${at(before)} order by received_at, id limit ${limit}::int`)).map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The decisions whose statement mail is still pending and that were decided before `before`, oldest first. The decision caps bound how many there can be. */
export async function pendingAuthorMails(q: Runner, before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select id from decisions where author_mail = 'pending' and decided_at < ${at(before)} order by decided_at, id`)).map((row) => row.id);
}

/**
 * The daily release, through the database's one function for it: every item answered before the cut-off is released with
 * its outcome as of the cut-off, and every released item whose outcome a review or a correction changed before it gets
 * its new outcome. The function refuses a cut-off in the database's future; a cut-off its clock has not reached yet (the
 * API's clock running ahead of it) is therefore taken as now. Answers how many items it changed.
 */
export async function releaseOutcomes(q: Runner, cutoff: Date): Promise<number> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ n: number }>(q, sql`select public.release_outcomes(least(${at(cutoff)}, now())) as n`);
  return row!.n;
}

/**
 * The contacts whose notice is still owed something: an item unanswered (a re-examination included), an item's outcome
 * mail pending or a changed outcome waiting for its release, or its receipt pending or folded. A line or a receipt that
 * was given up is owed nothing more.
 */
export async function contactsOwed(q: Runner): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ contact_id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select distinct n.contact_id from intakes n
         where n.contact_id is not null
           and (n.receipt in ('pending', 'folded')
                or exists (select 1 from intake_items i where i.intake_id = n.id and (i.outcome is null or i.outcome_mail = 'pending' or i.revision_pending_at is not null)))`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => row.contact_id);
}

/** One released item whose outcome mail is pending, with what its line's words follow from. */
export interface OutcomeLineRow {
  id: string;
  intakeId: string;
  ref: string;
  contactId: string | null;
  reporterId: string | null;
  position: number;
  targetType: TargetType;
  targetId: string;
  namedHandle: string | null;
  hasCase: boolean;
  suspect: boolean;
  shownOutcome: string;
  changed: boolean;
  reexamines: boolean;
  /** A decision answered it: a link that named nothing was answered without one. */
  byDecision: boolean;
  reexamined: boolean;
  ruleId: string | null;
  rulesVersion: number | null;
  decisionUnseen: boolean;
  /** The answering decision holds a seal. */
  sealed: boolean;
  /** 3e: the answering decision retires the handle of the account the item is about. */
  retired: boolean;
  /** 3e: the answering decision suspends or terminates that account. */
  measure: boolean;
  /** Every measure of the answering decision changed nothing when it was imposed. */
  noEffect: boolean;
  /** For an item about a post: the post quotes another. */
  quotes: boolean;
}

/** Every released item whose outcome mail is still pending, whichever round released it, by notice and position. */
export async function pendingOutcomeLines(q: Runner): Promise<OutcomeLineRow[]> {
  const found = await rows<Record<string, unknown>>(
    q,
    sql`select i.id, i.intake_id, n.ref, n.contact_id, i.reporter_account_id, i.position, i.target_type, i.target_id, i.named_handle, i.case_id is not null as has_case, i.suspect,
               i.shown_outcome, i.revised_sent_at is not null as changed, i.reexamines_item_id is not null as reexamines, i.answered_by is not null as by_decision,
               exists (select 1 from intake_items r where r.reexamines_item_id = i.id) as reexamined,
               d.rule_id, d.rules_version, coalesce(d.unseen, false) as decision_unseen,
               exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = i.answered_by and a.kind = 'seal_media') as sealed,
               exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = i.answered_by and a.kind = 'retire_handle') as retired,
               exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = i.answered_by and a.kind in ('suspend', 'terminate')) as measure,
               ${answerChangedNothing} as no_effect,
               coalesce((select p.quote_of_id is not null from posts p where i.target_type = 'post' and p.id = i.target_id), false) as quotes
          from intake_items i join intakes n on n.id = i.intake_id left join decisions d on d.id = i.answered_by
         where i.outcome_sent_at is not null and i.outcome_mail = 'pending' and i.shown_outcome is not null
         order by n.received_at, n.id, i.position, i.created_at, i.id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({
    id: row.id as string,
    intakeId: row.intake_id as string,
    ref: row.ref as string,
    contactId: row.contact_id as string | null,
    reporterId: row.reporter_account_id as string | null,
    position: row.position as number,
    targetType: row.target_type as TargetType,
    targetId: row.target_id as string,
    namedHandle: row.named_handle as string | null,
    hasCase: row.has_case as boolean,
    suspect: row.suspect as boolean,
    shownOutcome: row.shown_outcome as string,
    changed: row.changed as boolean,
    reexamines: row.reexamines as boolean,
    byDecision: row.by_decision as boolean,
    reexamined: row.reexamined as boolean,
    ruleId: row.rule_id as string | null,
    rulesVersion: row.rules_version as number | null,
    decisionUnseen: row.decision_unseen as boolean,
    sealed: row.sealed as boolean,
    retired: row.retired as boolean,
    measure: row.measure as boolean,
    noEffect: row.no_effect as boolean,
    quotes: row.quotes as boolean,
  }));
}

/** The notices of signed-out notifiers whose receipt the 24-hour cap folded: each rides in its address's next update. */
export async function foldedReceipts(q: Runner): Promise<NoticeRow[]> {
  const found = await rows<NoticeColumns>(q, sql`select ${noticeColumns} from intakes where receipt = 'folded' and contact_id is not null order by received_at, id`);
  return found.flatMap((row) => noticeOf(row) ?? []);
}

/** Records what became of these items' outcome mails, only where one is still pending. */
export async function recordOutcomeMails(q: Runner, itemIds: readonly string[], state: MailState): Promise<void> {
  if (itemIds.length === 0) return;
  await q.execute(sql`update intake_items set outcome_mail = ${state}::delivery_state where id = any(${uuids(itemIds)}) and outcome_mail = 'pending'`);
}

/** Records what became of a receipt that rode in an update, only while it is still pending or folded. */
export async function recordCarriedReceipt(q: Runner, intakeId: string, state: MailState): Promise<void> {
  await q.execute(
    sql`update intakes set receipt = ${state}::delivery_state, receipt_sent_at = case when ${state}::text = 'sent' then now() else receipt_sent_at end
         where id = ${intakeId}::uuid and receipt in ('pending', 'folded')`,
  );
}

/** A decision that holds an announced suspension or termination, as a condition on decision `d`. */
const HOLDS_ANNOUNCED = sql`exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind::text in ('suspend', 'terminate') and a.announced)`;

/**
 * The receipts and the statement mails still unsent `days` days after they were due, recorded as given up; answers their
 * ids. 3e (design, section 7.14 item 3): the statement mail of a decision that holds an announced measure is left out:
 * its outcome fixes the measure's start, so each is given up alone, under its subject's profile lock (giveUpAnnouncedMail).
 */
export async function giveUpReceiptsAndAuthorMails(q: Runner, now: Date, days: number): Promise<{ receipts: string[]; authorMails: string[] }> {
  const due = sql`${at(now)} - make_interval(days => ${days}::int)`;
  const receipts = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`update intakes set receipt = 'failed' where receipt in ('pending', 'folded') and received_at < ${due} returning id`);
  // 3f: a mail is owed from the time it became owed, which for a notice released after a hold is its informed_at, and for
  // the mail that an order's notice grew the newest record of the authority's words: never from the decision's own time,
  // which may be weeks before.
  const owedSince = sql.raw(`greatest(d.decided_at, coalesce(d.informed_at, d.decided_at),
      coalesce((select max(e.at) from public.legal_order_items i join public.legal_order_events e on e.order_id = i.order_id and e.kind = 'texts_recorded'
                 where i.id = d.order_item_id), d.decided_at))`);
  const authorMails = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`update decisions d set author_mail = 'failed' where d.author_mail = 'pending' and ${owedSince} < ${due} and not ${HOLDS_ANNOUNCED} returning d.id`);
  return { receipts: receipts.map((row) => row.id), authorMails: authorMails.map((row) => row.id) };
}

/** The statement mails of decisions that hold an announced measure, still unsent `days` days after the decision, with each decision's subject: each is given up alone. */
export async function announcedMailsDue(q: Runner, now: Date, days: number): Promise<{ decisionId: string; subjectId: string }[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string; subject: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select d.id, (select a.subject_account_id from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind::text in ('suspend', 'terminate')) as subject
          from decisions d where d.author_mail = 'pending' and d.decided_at < ${at(now)} - make_interval(days => ${days}::int) and ${HOLDS_ANNOUNCED}
         order by d.decided_at, d.id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({ decisionId: row.id, subjectId: row.subject }));
}

/**
 * Gives up one announced measure's statement mail, in a transaction whose caller took the subject's profile row first
 * (the lock order, item 4): the decision's row is updated only while its mail is still pending, and the database stamps
 * the time and fixes the start from it (decisions_mail_forward, decisions_mail_standing). True when this call gave it up.
 */
export async function giveUpAnnouncedMail(tx: DbTx, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`update decisions set author_mail = 'failed' where id = ${decisionId}::uuid and author_mail = 'pending' returning id`)).length > 0;
}

/** The outcome lines still unsent `days` days after their release, or after the release of their changed outcome, recorded as given up; answers their ids. */
export async function giveUpOutcomeMails(q: Runner, now: Date, days: number): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`update intake_items set outcome_mail = 'failed'
         where outcome_mail = 'pending' and coalesce(revised_sent_at, outcome_sent_at) < ${at(now)} - make_interval(days => ${days}::int) returning id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** An unanswered item in the urgent lane that has waited long enough to be alerted about again, with what decides whether it still calls for someone. */
export interface UrgentItemRow {
  caseId: string;
  targetType: TargetType;
  targetId: string;
  suspect: boolean;
  /** When the item arrived, in epoch milliseconds. */
  arrivedMs: number;
  /** Whether a decision taken while deciding, a note, or a recorded choice not to seal came after the item arrived. */
  interimAfter: boolean;
  noteAfter: boolean;
  declinedAfter: boolean;
  /** When the newest recorded choice not to seal of the case was saved, in epoch milliseconds, to the millisecond. */
  newestDeclinedMs: number | null;
  /** A post case's post is not visible: withheld, removed, or deleted by its author. */
  postHidden: boolean;
}

/**
 * The unanswered items of open cases in the urgent lane that arrived before `before`, the cases that have waited longest
 * first and each case's items together. "After the item arrived" compares the item's time with the decision's or the
 * text's, as the view of measures in force does: no later than.
 */
export async function urgentItems(q: Runner, before: Date): Promise<UrgentItemRow[]> {
  const after = (kind: string) => sql.raw(`exists (select 1 from staff_texts t where t.case_id = c.id and t.kind = '${kind}' and t.created_at >= i.created_at)`);
  const found = await rows<Record<string, unknown>>(
    q,
    sql`select c.id as case_id, c.target_type, c.target_id, i.suspect,
               floor(extract(epoch from i.created_at) * 1000)::float8 as arrived_ms,
               exists (select 1 from decisions d where d.case_id = c.id and d.kind = 'interim' and d.decided_at >= i.created_at) as interim_after,
               ${after("note")} as note_after, ${after("seal_declined")} as declined_after,
               (select floor(extract(epoch from max(t.created_at)) * 1000)::float8 from staff_texts t where t.case_id = c.id and t.kind = 'seal_declined') as newest_declined_ms,
               coalesce((select p.state <> 'visible' from posts p where c.target_type = 'post' and p.id = c.target_id), false) as post_hidden
          from intake_items i join cases c on c.id = i.case_id
         where c.closed_at is null and i.lane = 0 and i.outcome is null and i.created_at < ${at(before)}
         order by c.oldest_open_at, c.id, i.seq`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({
    caseId: row.case_id as string,
    targetType: row.target_type as TargetType,
    targetId: row.target_id as string,
    suspect: row.suspect as boolean,
    arrivedMs: Number(row.arrived_ms),
    interimAfter: row.interim_after as boolean,
    noteAfter: row.note_after as boolean,
    declinedAfter: row.declined_after as boolean,
    newestDeclinedMs: row.newest_declined_ms === null ? null : Number(row.newest_declined_ms),
    postHidden: row.post_hidden as boolean,
  }));
}

/**
 * The cases past their lane's response time (24 hours in lanes 0 and 1, seven days in lane 2, counted from the oldest
 * unanswered item), per lane with the oldest one's time, and the open cases that have held a measure taken while
 * deciding for more than 24 hours, whatever their lane.
 */
export async function waitingCases(q: Runner, now: Date): Promise<{ lanes: { lane: Lane; count: number; oldest: Date }[]; interim: number; replies: { count: number; oldest: Date } | null }> {
  const found = await rows<{ lane: Lane; n: number; oldest: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select lane, count(*)::int as n, ${iso("min(oldest_open_at)")} as oldest from cases
         where closed_at is null and oldest_open_at < ${at(now)} - case when lane = 2 then interval '7 days' else interval '24 hours' end
         group by lane order by lane`,
  );
  const [held] = await rows<{ n: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(distinct m.case_id)::int as n from measures_in_force m join decisions d on d.id = m.decision_id join cases c on c.id = m.case_id
         where m.decision_kind = 'interim' and c.closed_at is null and d.decided_at < ${at(now)} - interval '24 hours'`,
  );
  // 3e (design, section 7.14): the replies to a suspension or a termination that no decision answered for longer than
  // korbat's aim, with the oldest one's time.
  const [replies] = await rows<{ n: number; oldest: string | null }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n, ${iso("min(r.filed_at)")} as oldest from suspension_replies r
         where r.answered_by is null and r.filed_at < ${at(now)} - make_interval(hours => ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS}::int)`,
  );
  return {
    lanes: found.map((row) => ({ lane: row.lane, count: row.n, oldest: new Date(row.oldest) })),
    interim: held!.n,
    replies: replies!.n > 0 && replies!.oldest !== null ? { count: replies!.n, oldest: new Date(replies!.oldest) } : null,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- retention

/**
 * The SQL of the retention job and of the overview's late erasures (3c design, sections 6.4, 7.3 and 7.9). Every time is
 * the database's own: each erase function checks its due rule against the database's now(), so the job asks with the same
 * clock, and one clock decides what is due. The periods are the contracts' RETENTION, handed over as numbers.
 *
 * The candidates are read from the partial indexes that hold only what is left to erase, so a round's work follows what
 * is left, never every case ever closed. The freeze is read here only to keep a case that holds nothing but snapshots of
 * a frozen post out of the candidates: for every snapshot the one function that erases one decides.
 */

/** The cases that hold a row erase_case_evidence would change: an unerased snapshot that is not of a frozen post, an unerased note or draft, an appeal statement, or an unreleased hold. */
const CANDIDATE_CASES = sql`
  select s.case_id from evidence_snapshots s where s.erased_at is null and not (s.target_type = 'post' and public.post_frozen(s.target_id))
  union select t.case_id from staff_texts t where t.confirmed_at is null and t.erased_at is null
  union select d.case_id from appeals a join decisions d on d.id = a.decision_id where a.statement is not null
  union select h.case_id from media_holds h where h.released_at is null`;

/** A final decision citing R4 that is not redacted yet and one of whose R4 measures is in force, as `d`. */
const REDACTABLE = sql`d.kind = 'final' and d.rule_id = 'R4' and d.redacted_at is null
  and exists (select 1 from measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = d.id and m.kind in ('remove', 'remove_media', 'reset_bio', 'reset_display_name'))`;

/** A decision one of whose statement texts is unerased, as `d`, joined to the profile `p` of its case's subject. */
const STATEMENT_HELD = sql`from decisions d
  join cases c on c.id = d.case_id
  join profiles p on p.id = case when c.target_type = 'account' then c.target_id else (select x.author_id from posts x where x.id = c.target_id) end
  where exists (select 1 from staff_texts t where t.digest in (d.facts_digest, d.reason_digest, d.legal_reference_digest) and t.erased_at is null)`;

/** The candidate cases whose evidence is due now, in id order. */
export async function dueCases(q: Runner): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select k.case_id as id from (${CANDIDATE_CASES}) k where public.case_evidence_due_at(k.case_id) <= now() order by 1`);
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The unerased intakes whose record is due now. None is due before `days` days after it was received, which the index is read by. */
export async function dueIntakes(q: Runner, days: number): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select n.id from intakes n where n.erased_at is null and n.received_at <= now() - make_interval(days => ${days}::int) and public.intake_due_at(n.id) <= now() order by n.received_at, n.id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The R4 decisions that are final for their author and not redacted yet. The redaction itself answers false for one whose post is frozen. */
export async function dueRedactions(q: Runner): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select d.id from decisions d where ${REDACTABLE} and public.decision_final_at(d.id) <= now() order by d.decided_at, d.id`);
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The decisions that still hold a statement text and whose subject's profile was deleted at least `months` months ago. */
export async function dueStatements(q: Runner, months: number): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select d.id ${STATEMENT_HELD} and p.deleted_at <= now() - make_interval(months => ${months}::int) order by d.decided_at, d.id`);
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

const changedBy = async (q: Runner, call: ReturnType<typeof sql>): Promise<number> => (await rows<{ n: number }>(q, sql`select ${call} as n`))[0]!.n;

/** Deletes the drafts nobody confirmed that are older than `hours` hours; never a note, a recorded choice not to seal or a confirmed text. */
export const sweepStaffTexts = (q: Runner, hours: number) => changedBy(q, sql`public.sweep_staff_texts(now() - make_interval(hours => ${hours}::int))`);
/** Erases a due case's snapshots (never one of a frozen post), notes, drafts and appeal statements, and releases its holds. */
export const eraseCaseEvidence = (q: Runner, caseId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_case_evidence(${caseId}::uuid)`);
/** Erases a due intake's record: its explanation, its cited law, who sent it and its re-examinations' statements. */
export const eraseIntake = (q: Runner, intakeId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_intake(${intakeId}::uuid)`);
/** Erases the statement texts of a decision whose subject's account has been deleted for 12 months. */
export const eraseStatementTexts = (q: Runner, decisionId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_statement_texts(${decisionId}::uuid)`);
/** Deletes the access rows older than `months` months, erasing first the reveal reasons they name. */
export const deleteAccessLog = (q: Runner, months: number) => changedBy(q, sql`public.delete_access_log(now() - make_interval(months => ${months}::int))`);
/** Forgets that a deleted account sent its reports; 0 for an account whose auth row is not marked deleted. */
export const forgetReporter = (q: Runner, accountId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.forget_reporter(${accountId}::uuid)`);
/**
 * 3e: erases the text of every reply to a suspension or a termination that is answered and whose decision is final for
 * its author, keeping its digest and its row; an unanswered reply keeps its text however old. Answers how many it erased.
 */
export const eraseReplyStatements = (q: Runner) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_reply_statements()`);
/** 3e: deletes the marks and the tallies of reports sent on a UTC day before the frame of the reporting counts; answers how many rows. */
export const forgetReportCounts = (q: Runner) => changedBy(q, sql`public.forget_report_counts()`);

/** Makes an R4 restriction's erasure final; false when it changed nothing (its post is frozen, or another round was faster). */
export async function redactR4(q: Runner, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await rows<{ done: boolean }>(q, sql`select public.redact_r4_body(${decisionId}::uuid) as done`))[0]!.done;
}

/** The overview's late erasures that this module's tables answer: what each step should have changed more than a day ago. */
export interface LateErasures {
  caseEvidence: number;
  intakeRecords: number;
  statements: number;
  redactions: number;
  drafts: number;
  accessLog: number;
}

/**
 * How much each due rule is late by more than a day. A case that holds only snapshots of a frozen post is no candidate
 * and never counted, and a redaction whose post is frozen would change nothing now, so it is not counted either: both
 * wait for an admin's answer, not for the job.
 */
export async function lateErasures(q: Runner, periods: { intakeDays: number; statementMonths: number; draftHours: number; accessLogMonths: number }): Promise<LateErasures> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ case_evidence: number; intake_records: number; statements: number; redactions: number; drafts: number; access_log: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select
      (select count(*)::int from (${CANDIDATE_CASES}) k where public.case_evidence_due_at(k.case_id) < now() - interval '1 day') as case_evidence,
      (select count(*)::int from intakes n
        where n.erased_at is null and n.received_at <= now() - make_interval(days => ${periods.intakeDays}::int) and public.intake_due_at(n.id) < now() - interval '1 day') as intake_records,
      (select count(*)::int ${STATEMENT_HELD} and p.deleted_at < now() - make_interval(months => ${periods.statementMonths}::int) - interval '1 day') as statements,
      (select count(*)::int from decisions d join cases c on c.id = d.case_id
        where ${REDACTABLE} and public.decision_final_at(d.id) < now() - interval '1 day'
          and not (c.target_type = 'post' and public.post_frozen(c.target_id))) as redactions,
      (select count(*)::int from staff_texts t
        where t.kind not in ('note', 'seal_declined') and t.confirmed_at is null and t.created_at < now() - make_interval(hours => ${periods.draftHours}::int) - interval '1 day') as drafts,
      (select count(*)::int from case_access_log l where l.at < now() - make_interval(months => ${periods.accessLogMonths}::int) - interval '1 day') as access_log`,
  );
  return { caseEvidence: row!.case_evidence, intakeRecords: row!.intake_records, statements: row!.statements, redactions: row!.redactions, drafts: row!.drafts, accessLog: row!.access_log };
}
```

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Image } from "expo-image";
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { useReducedMotion } from "react-native-reanimated";
import { isHiddenMedia, type HiddenMedia, type MediaView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { API_BASE } from "@/lib/api";
import { CHIP_WORDS } from "@/lib/moderation-words";
import { HiddenImage, HiddenRowWords, HiddenThumbnail, hiddenImageWords } from "./HiddenImage";
import { ImageFaultView, useImageFault } from "./ImageFault";
import { MediaViewer } from "./MediaViewer";

/** A single image keeps its own shape, within limits, so a very tall or very wide one cannot take over the timeline. */
const MIN_RATIO = 3 / 4;
const MAX_RATIO = 2;
const FRAME_RATIO = 16 / 9;
const GAP = 2;
const THUMBNAIL = 64;

export const clampRatio = (width: number, height: number): number => Math.min(MAX_RATIO, Math.max(MIN_RATIO, width / height));

/**
 * The small size of an image with its blurhash; expo-image loads it lazily on the web. The blurhash
 * fades into the image unless the system asks for reduced motion, which swaps it at once.
 */
function Picture({ item, style, onError }: { item: MediaView; style: { width: number | "100%"; height: number | "100%"; borderRadius?: number }; onError?: () => void }) {
  const still = useReducedMotion();
  return (
    // On the web expo-image takes the <img alt> from accessibilityLabel, not from alt.
    <Image source={{ uri: `${API_BASE}${item.small}` }} placeholder={{ blurhash: item.blurhash }} contentFit="cover" transition={still ? 0 : 150} accessibilityLabel={item.alt} style={style} onError={onError} />
  );
}

/**
 * The label on the author's own image that moderation withheld or removed (3c design, section 9): the author keeps seeing
 * such an image, and reads on the image itself that others do not. The API marks an image so only for its author.
 */
export function OwnImageLabel({ state }: { state: NonNullable<MediaView["moderation"]> }) {
  const amber = state === "withheld";
  return (
    <View pointerEvents="none" className={`absolute left-1 top-1 rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 ${amber ? "bg-amber-950" : "bg-red-950"}`}>
      <Text className={`text-xs font-medium ${amber ? "text-amber-300" : "text-red-300"}`}>{amber ? CHIP_WORDS.underReview : CHIP_WORDS.removed}</Text>
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * One image of the frame: the control that opens it and, beside that control, the label of the author's own restricted
 * image, as text of its own. 3d: when an image of the reader's own post fails to load, its status is asked once, and an
 * image being restored or lost shows why in its place, with nothing to open.
 */
function Cell({ item, onPress, own }: { item: MediaView; onPress: () => void; own: boolean }) {
  const { fault, onError } = useImageFault(item.id, own);
  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      {fault !== null ? (
        <ImageFaultView fault={fault} />
      ) : (
        <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel={`Open image: ${item.alt}`} onPress={onPress} style={{ flex: 1 }}>
          <Picture item={item} style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%" }} onError={onError} />
        </Pressable>
      )}
      {item.moderation ? <OwnImageLabel state={item.moderation} /> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * The images of a post. One image is shown in its own ratio; two to four share a 16:9 frame and are
 * cropped to their cell. Pressing one opens the viewer; ALT shows the descriptions in place. An image
 * moderation hid from this reader keeps its place as a placeholder: it has no size of its own, so alone
 * it takes the frame's ratio, it is no control, and it has no description to show. The viewer is told the
 * post that holds the images, so that an image can be reported on it, unless the post is the reader's own.
 */
function Grid({ media, postId, own }: { media: (MediaView | HiddenMedia)[]; postId?: string; own?: boolean }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [described, setDescribed] = useState(false);
  const cell = (index: number) => {
    const item = media[index]!;
    return isHiddenMedia(item) ? <HiddenImage key={item.id} item={item} /> : <Cell key={item.id} item={item} onPress={() => setOpen(index)} own={own === true} />;
  };
  const first = media[0]!;
  // Descriptions exist only for the images this reader is shown.
  const anyShown = media.some((item) => !isHiddenMedia(item));

  let frame;
  if (media.length === 1) {
    frame = <View style={{ aspectRatio: isHiddenMedia(first) ? FRAME_RATIO : clampRatio(first.width, first.height) }}>{cell(0)}</View>;
  } else if (media.length === 2) {
    frame = <View style={{ aspectRatio: FRAME_RATIO, flexDirection: "row", gap: GAP }}>{[cell(0), cell(1)]}</View>;
  } else if (media.length === 3) {
    frame = (
      <View style={{ aspectRatio: FRAME_RATIO, flexDirection: "row", gap: GAP }}>
        {cell(0)}
        <View style={{ flex: 1, gap: GAP }}>{[cell(1), cell(2)]}</View>
      </View>
    );
  } else {
    frame = (
      <View style={{ aspectRatio: FRAME_RATIO, gap: GAP }}>
        <View style={{ flex: 1, flexDirection: "row", gap: GAP }}>{[cell(0), cell(1)]}</View>
        <View style={{ flex: 1, flexDirection: "row", gap: GAP }}>{[cell(2), cell(3)]}</View>
      </View>
    );
  }

  return (
    <View className="mt-2">
      <View className="overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-zinc-800">{frame}</View>
      {anyShown ? (
        <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" aria-expanded={described} accessibilityLabel={described ? "Hide image descriptions" : "Show image descriptions"} onPress={() => setDescribed(!described)} className="mt-1 self-start rounded border border-zinc-700 px-1.5 py-0.5">
          <Text className="text-xs font-semibold text-zinc-300">ALT</Text>
        </Pressable>
      ) : null}
      {described
        ? media.map((item, index) => (
            <Text key={item.id} className="mt-1 text-sm leading-5 text-zinc-300">
              {media.length > 1 ? `${index + 1}. ` : ""}
              {/* A hidden image keeps its number, so the others' numbers match their places in the frame. */}
              {isHiddenMedia(item) ? hiddenImageWords(item) : item.alt}
            </Text>
          ))
        : null}
      {open === null ? null : <MediaViewer media={media} index={open} onIndex={setOpen} onClose={() => setOpen(null)} postId={own ? undefined : postId} own={own === true} />}
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * A post's images (`Grid`), or a quoted post's as one row of small squares (`compact`). The squares
 * are pictures, not buttons: the whole quote is a link to the quoted post, where the grid and the
 * viewer are, and a control inside another control is one that assistive technology cannot reach.
 * A hidden image keeps its square in the row, and the row says the placeholder's sentence once, as
 * text, under the squares. `postId` is the post that holds the images and `own` says that the reader
 * wrote it: the viewer reports an image on that post, and offers no report of the reader's own.
 */
export function MediaGrid({ media, compact = false, postId, own = false }: { media: (MediaView | HiddenMedia)[]; compact?: boolean; postId?: string; own?: boolean }) {
  if (media.length === 0) return null;
  if (!compact) return <Grid media={media} postId={postId} own={own} />;
  return (
    <View className="mt-2">
      <View className="flex-row" style={{ gap: GAP }}>
        {media.map((item) => (isHiddenMedia(item) ? <HiddenThumbnail key={item.id} size={THUMBNAIL} /> : <Picture key={item.id} item={item} style={{ width: THUMBNAIL, height: THUMBNAIL, borderRadius: 6 }} />))}
      </View>
      <HiddenRowWords media={media} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { useEffect } from "react";
import { Image } from "expo-image";
import { Modal, Platform, Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import { useReducedMotion } from "react-native-reanimated";
import { isHiddenMedia, type HiddenMedia, type MediaView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { API_BASE } from "@/lib/api";
import { reportHref } from "@/lib/moderation";
import { CHIP_WORDS, REPORT_WORDS } from "@/lib/moderation-words";
import { HiddenImage } from "./HiddenImage";
import { ImageFaultView, useImageFault } from "./ImageFault";

interface MediaViewerProps {
  media: (MediaView | HiddenMedia)[];
  index: number;
  onIndex: (index: number) => void;
  onClose: () => void;
  /** The post that holds the images: an image is reported on it. Absent for the reader's own post, which they do not report. */
  postId?: string;
  /** 3d: the reader wrote the post, so an image that fails to load asks its status once and says why it is missing. */
  own?: boolean;
}

/**
 * What the viewer shows: one image in its large size, fitted inside the screen, with its description
 * underneath, its place among the post's images and the controls. The viewer is opened from an image's
 * own cell only; stepping through the post's images can still come to one moderation hid from this
 * reader, which is never loaded: its placeholder stands in the image's place. An image that is shown can
 * be reported from here, on the post that holds it; the author's own withheld or removed image says so.
 */
export function MediaViewerContent({ media, index, onIndex, onClose, postId, own = false }: MediaViewerProps) {
  const still = useReducedMotion();
  const item = media[index]!;
  const { fault, onError } = useImageFault(item.id, own && !isHiddenMedia(item));
  const many = media.length > 1;
  const step = (by: number) => onIndex((index + by + media.length) % media.length);

  return (
    <View className="flex-1 bg-black/95">
      <View className="flex-row items-center justify-between px-4 py-3">
        <Text className="text-sm text-zinc-300">{many ? `${index + 1} of ${media.length}` : ""}</Text>
        <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Close the image viewer" onPress={onClose} className="rounded-lg border border-zinc-700 px-3 py-1.5">
          <Text className="text-sm text-zinc-200">Close</Text>
        </Pressable>
      </View>
      <View className="flex-1 px-2">
        {isHiddenMedia(item) ? (
          <HiddenImage item={item} />
        ) : fault !== null ? (
          <ImageFaultView fault={fault} />
        ) : (
          <Image source={{ uri: `${API_BASE}${item.large}` }} placeholder={{ blurhash: item.blurhash }} contentFit="contain" transition={still ? 0 : 150} accessibilityLabel={item.alt} style={{ flex: 1 }} onError={onError} />
        )}
      </View>
      {isHiddenMedia(item) ? null : <Text className="px-4 py-3 text-center text-sm leading-5 text-zinc-200">{item.alt}</Text>}
      {!isHiddenMedia(item) && item.moderation ? (
        <Text className={`pb-3 text-center text-sm font-medium ${item.moderation === "withheld" ? "text-amber-300" : "text-red-300"}`}>
          {item.moderation === "withheld" ? CHIP_WORDS.underReview : CHIP_WORDS.removed}
        </Text>
      ) : null}
      {!isHiddenMedia(item) && postId ? (
        // A real anchor, as every link of the app; the viewer closes as the form opens.
        <Link href={reportHref({ post: postId, media: item.id })} onPress={onClose} asChild>
          <Pressable className="self-center pb-3">
            <Text className="text-sm text-zinc-400 underline">{REPORT_WORDS.imageControl}</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </Link>
      ) : null}
      {many ? (
        <View className="flex-row justify-center gap-3 pb-4">
          <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Previous image" onPress={() => step(-1)} className="rounded-lg border border-zinc-700 px-4 py-2">
            <Text className="text-sm text-zinc-200">Previous</Text>
          </Pressable>
          <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Next image" onPress={() => step(1)} className="rounded-lg border border-zinc-700 px-4 py-2">
            <Text className="text-sm text-zinc-200">Next</Text>
          </Pressable>
        </View>
      ) : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * One image on the whole screen. Arrow keys move between the images of the post; react-native-web's
 * Modal closes it on Escape and returns focus to the image that opened it. It appears at once: nothing
 * about it needs motion, and the image fades in from its blurhash only when reduced motion is not asked for.
 */
export function MediaViewer({ media, index, onIndex, onClose, postId, own }: MediaViewerProps) {
  const many = media.length > 1;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (Platform.OS !== "web") return;
    const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (event.key === "ArrowRight" && many) onIndex((index + 1) % media.length);
      if (event.key === "ArrowLeft" && many) onIndex((index - 1 + media.length) % media.length);
    };
    document.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
    return () => document.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
  }, [index, many, media.length, onIndex]);

  return (
    <Modal visible transparent animationType="none" onRequestClose={onClose}>
      <MediaViewerContent media={media} index={index} onIndex={onIndex} onClose={onClose} postId={postId} own={own} />
    </Modal>
  );
}
```

```ts
  rateLimited: (wait: string, contact: string) =>
    `korbat cannot take another report from this network or account right now: it takes at most ${NOTICE_LIMITS.signedOut.perHour} reports an hour and ${NOTICE_LIMITS.signedOut.perDay} a day without an account, and ${NOTICE_LIMITS.signedIn.perHour} an hour and ${NOTICE_LIMITS.signedIn.perDay} a day with one. Try again in about ${wait}, or ${MAIL_INSTEAD(contact)}`,
  unavailable: (contact: string) => `korbat cannot take reports right now. Try again in a few minutes, or ${MAIL_INSTEAD(contact)}`,

const OUTSIDE_KORBAT = "go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live.";

export const STATUS_WORDS = {
  title: "Your report",
  reference: (ref: string) => `Reference ${ref}`,
  received: (time: string) => `Received on ${time}.`,
  item: (n: number) => `Item ${n}`,

  decided: (day: string) => `Decided on ${day}:`,

  reexaminationOpen: (until: string) => `A moderator decides it again as a new report. You can ask once for each item, within six months of being told, until ${until}.`,
  /** The control beside such an item: its button, its optional statement, and what it says once asked. */
  reexamine: "Ask for a re-examination",

  /** Beside an outcome a review or a correction changed, and a re-examination's answer. */

  courts: `You can ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,

  confirmed: "This address is confirmed as the sender's.",

  stopped: "korbat's report emails to this address are stopped.",
  undo: "Undo: email this address about reports again",
  retry: "Try again",
} as const;

/**
 * The day's limits of the two forms that ask korbat to look again, an appeal and a re-examination (3c design, section
 * 7.7): worded with their number and the wait the answer gives, since the wait can be a whole day. An appeal is counted
 * per account; a re-examination per account, and without one per network.
 */
export const DAILY_LIMIT_WORDS = {
  appeals: (wait: string) => `korbat takes at most ${DAILY_LIMITS.appeals} appeals a day from one account. Try again in about ${wait}.`,
  reexaminations: (wait: string) => `korbat takes at most ${DAILY_LIMITS.reexaminations} requests for a re-examination a day from one account, or without an account from one network. Try again in about ${wait}.`,
};

export const CASES_WORDS = {
  nav: "Cases",
  title: "Cases",
  tabs: { about: "About you", reports: "Your reports" },

export const DECISION_WORDS = {
  title: "korbat's decision",
  back: "All cases",
  statement: "Statement of reasons",

  empty: "(empty)",

/** The chip on the author's own withheld or removed post, and the labels on their own images. */
export const CHIP_WORDS = {

} as const;

/**

/** The terms page's Contact section, built from the build's contact address; it is not part of the terms' own sections. */
export const CONTACT_WORDS = {

```

### Replace `infra/compose.yml` (whole file)

```yaml
name: korbat

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options: { max-size: "20m", max-file: "5" }

x-node-common: &node-common
  restart: unless-stopped
  read_only: true
  tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging: *logging

services:
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL 18. From 18 on the image keeps the cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/<major>/docker, so
    # the volume is mounted one level up and a later major can pg_upgrade inside it. A cluster from the
    # earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) is moved over by scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs.
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32fbca283dc835b0596f4e52b51b4c6662d7810b2f4084f60a1873
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 1g
    memswap_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}
      # The contact point's watcher's role (3f), which 01-roles.sh makes on a new data directory. Not required: a stack
      # without the watcher runs without it.
      KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}
    volumes:
      - pgdata18:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    # watch: the watcher's own network to the database, which holds nothing else.
    networks: [data, watch]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    # Valkey, the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, under the service name the URLs already use. A password
    # is required: nothing on the data network may read the session cache without it.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 384m
    memswap_limit: 384m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    volumes:
    # A fresh volume: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into `redisdata`, and that
    # volume held only transient state (limits, codes in flight, cached sessions, queued image jobs).
      - valkeydata:/data
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    <<: *node-common
    restart: "no"
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: postgres://korbat_migrate:${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/migrations
      # `staff.js enroll` runs here, as the migrator, the one role the running API never holds, and records on each link
      # the console's origin and relying party ID it is issued for. Empty, the console is off and enroll refuses.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # 3f: staff.js order-open runs here too, and reads the home state (whether an order is cross-border) and the app's
      # origin (how a link is read, as the console's route reads it). Neither is required: enroll and the migrations run
      # without them, and order-open refuses with one sentence while either is empty.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:-}
    networks: [data]
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }

  api:
    <<: *node-common
    # The image's name, the one Compose gives it by default, written out: notify (3f) runs the same image, so it is
    # built once.
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
      args:
        KORBAT_VERSION: ${KORBAT_VERSION:-0.0.0}
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      # development or production, from infra/.env; production turns on the guards against test keys, plain-http
      # origins and a relay without TLS. The worker below always runs as production.
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
      PORT: "3000"
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_API: postgres://korbat_api:${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      DATABASE_URL_AUTH: postgres://korbat_auth:${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: ${API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-}
      # Which header names the client: the stack refuses to start without a choice.
      TRUST_PROXY: ${API_TRUST_PROXY:?set API_TRUST_PROXY in infra/.env}
      # Auth settings. The stack refuses to start while any of these is missing from infra/.env.
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:?set API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env}
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: ${API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY:?set API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY in infra/.env}
      IP_HASH_KEY: ${API_IP_HASH_KEY:?set API_IP_HASH_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEY: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEY:?set API_TOTP_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      # Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name and address; earlier keys stay accepted for decryption.
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY:?set API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY:?set API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in infra/.env}
      SMTP_URL: ${API_SMTP_URL:?set API_SMTP_URL in infra/.env}
      MAIL_FROM: ${API_MAIL_FROM:?set API_MAIL_FROM in infra/.env}
      TERMS_VERSION: ${API_TERMS_VERSION:?set API_TERMS_VERSION in infra/.env}
      # The verified badge's phone check. off (the default) hides the badge; vonage needs the two credentials.
      VERIFY_PROVIDER: ${API_VERIFY_PROVIDER:-off}
      VONAGE_API_KEY: ${API_VONAGE_API_KEY:-}
      VONAGE_API_SECRET: ${API_VONAGE_API_SECRET:-}
      VERIFY_BRAND: ${API_VERIFY_BRAND:-korbat}
      # Passkeys. Empty values leave the API's defaults: the host of APP_ORIGIN as the RP ID and korbat as the name.
      WEBAUTHN_RP_ID: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID:-}
      WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME:-}
      # The staff console, served by Caddy's second site: the origin staff open it at, and the RP ID staff keys are bound
      # to (empty means the console's hostname). An empty origin switches the console off: every /api/staff path then
      # answers 404. The migrate service gets the same two values for `staff.js enroll`.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # Moderation: the UTC hour of the daily release of decisions to those who reported, the queue's emergency switch, and
      # the retention job's switch, which is off only for a restore window (README, Restoring, step 5).
      MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: ${API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR:-7}
      MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: ${API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN:-off}
      MODERATION_RETENTION: ${API_MODERATION_RETENTION:-on}
      # Authorities' orders (3f): whether the alert tick judges the alert channel's health. Empty means on in production;
      # off until the contact point's mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
      NOTIFY: ${API_NOTIFY:-}
      # The operator's Member State, a state whose facts the contracts hold (DE is filled in), and the published contact
      # point for authorities. Both empty until the owner's list is done; the home state is required once the contact
      # point is set.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      CONTACT_POINT: ${API_CONTACT_POINT:-}
      # 3f Task 5: whether a deletion keeps an account's address, at most seven days, while a report of its sealed images
      # to the authorities is owed. Empty means on; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once.
      REPORT_HOLD: ${API_REPORT_HOLD:-}
      # Images. The API writes uploads and only reads what the worker stored.
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      MEDIA_RECONCILE: ${MEDIA_RECONCILE:-on}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
    networks: [app, data]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # The image worker runs the decoder, the most exploitable code in the stack. It has no network at
  # all, no credentials and no capabilities: it reads uploads and writes the store, and that is
  # everything it can reach. The memory limit was sized on worst-case images (2b design, Research).
  worker:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/worker/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 768m
    memswap_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 64
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=64m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads:ro
      - media-store:/media/store
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/media/store/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The contact point's watcher (3f design, section 5): the API's image with dist/notify.js, under the profile notify. It
  # reads the contact-point mailbox over IMAP and publishes the alerts to ntfy. On the network watch it reaches PostgreSQL
  # as korbat_notify, whose grants are four tables, and nothing else; on push it reaches ntfy. It never joins data, where
  # the API listens and the limit store is. It exits rather than hang, and Docker starts it again. No setting of it is
  # required by Compose: the program names the one it is missing and exits.
  notify:
    <<: *node-common
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["node", "dist/notify.js"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    # Measured in this image (3f Task 1): about 82 MB resident idle, a peak of 93 MB during a first read of 10,000 old
    # messages, which took 21 seconds and fell back to 81 MB; under this limit the container's peak was 85 MB, with no
    # kill. 128 MB keeps more than a third above that peak.
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:-production}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY: postgres://korbat_notify:${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_USER: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_USER:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK:-}
      NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN:-}
    # A fixed address on push (3f's review, operations3), which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
    # (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): ntfy lets any one address publish 60 times and then once every 5 seconds (lab
    # L1), which would hold an order's alert behind a flood of contact mail. It lies inside PUSH_SUBNET, at the top of
    # the range, which Docker hands out last; change it, and the file's line, with the subnet.
    networks:
      watch: {}
      push:
        ipv4_address: ${NOTIFY_PUSH_IP:-172.16.91.254}
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      ntfy: { condition: service_started }
    # The watcher writes the time of every round it ends; two minutes without one is a hang.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - Number(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/korbat-notify-beat', 'utf8')) < 120000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # The hand-over of one seal's files (3f design, sections 5 and 7.14), under the profile handover, started by the operator
  # alone: docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests. The API's
  # image with dist/handover.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no credential, no capability,
  # the image store and (3d) the quarantine read-only, the quarantine looked in first. It has no bind mount here: the
  # directory for the archive is an argument of the command (an empty source would stop every Compose command of the
  # stack), on an encrypted volume owned by uid 1000, the image's user node, the only place it can write. No setting of
  # it is required.
  handover:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["handover"]
    command: ["node", "dist/handover.js"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro

  # The quarantine's mover (3d design, sections 5 and 7.1), under the profile quarantine, started by the operator alone:
  # docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt, with the list that
  # staff.js quarantine-list printed, and the receipt then recorded by staff.js quarantine-record (the README,
  # Quarantine). The API's image with dist/quarantine.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no
  # environment, no credential, no capability and a read-only root; the image store and the quarantine read-write, and
  # nothing else. Its two roots are arguments of its entry point, and it refuses to start without both; what follows the
  # service's name on the command line (--lost, --inventory) is appended to them. It is the one service that writes the
  # quarantine; handover reads it, and the api, migrate and worker services never mount it.
  quarantine:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["quarantine"]
    entrypoint: ["node", "dist/quarantine.js", "/media/store", "/media/quarantine"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine

  # The push server (3f design, section 5), under the profile notify, never linked into korbat's programs: ntfy at its
  # pinned release, reading its users, rights and tokens from infra/ntfy/server.yml (git-ignored, made from
  # server.yml.example), mounted read-only, since Compose would blank the $2a$10$ of a password hash in a variable. Only
  # on push, which is internal: it has no route out, so nothing is forwarded upstream. Its cache and auth files are on its
  # volume, at /var/tmp, the one directory of the image its user may write to.
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.28.0@sha256:6ef4b819f722fccdc036af611c4774cfdc2de821ab74fdd48bbf4c9d6f8973da
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["serve", "--config", "/etc/ntfy/server.yml"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy-data:/var/tmp
    networks: [push]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:2586/v1/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 4

  # Caddy serves the web app on port 8080, proxying /api, the staff console on port 8090, proxying only /api/staff, and
  # (3f) the phones' push site on port 8091, proxying only the two topics' subscriptions to ntfy. It runs as its own
  # user, sees only the API and ntfy, and is the only thing cloudflared can reach. A client from the push network (ntfy,
  # the watcher) is refused 403 on the app's and the console's sites.
  caddy:
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/caddy/Dockerfile
      args:
        EXPO_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY:?set WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in infra/.env}
        KORBAT_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
        TUNNEL: ${TUNNEL:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE: ${WEB_BADGE:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL:?set WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env}
        # 3f: the terms' contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State; neither is required (Before going public).
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT: ${WEB_CONTACT_POINT:-}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: ${WEB_HOME_STATE:-}
    depends_on:
      api: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      # The push network's subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse (3f).
      PUSH_SUBNET: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}
      # The app's site, open (the default) or closed: closed answers 503 to every path while a restore is checked (3f,
      # section 7.17). Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [edge, app, push]

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1@sha256:b269e8abd07a5bf6f3f4be65d5050b2174eca89c56a0241a8ff32a16aec454e4
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    profiles: ["tunnel"]
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks: [edge]
    depends_on:
      - caddy

# cloudflared reaches only Caddy, Caddy reaches only the API and ntfy, and the API alone reaches the data services, but
# for the watcher's own network to PostgreSQL (3f).
networks:
  edge:
  app:
  data:
  # The watcher and PostgreSQL, nothing else. Not internal: the mail host's port 993 is reached through its gateway.
  watch:
  # ntfy, the watcher and Caddy. Internal: no route out. Its fixed subnet is what the app's and the console's sites refuse.
  push:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}

volumes:
  # PostgreSQL 18. The earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) stays until scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs has
  # moved it and you remove it by hand.
  pgdata18:
  valkeydata:
  # Uploads wait here for the worker and are deleted once processed. Nothing in it needs a backup.
  media-uploads:
  # The images korbat serves. Back it up together with the database.
  media-store:
  # 3d: the files of images sealed for good, moved out of the store by the quarantine service, on the host's encrypted
  # disk. It is in no backup, by decision: a restore never brings a destroyed file back. Owned by uid 1000, mode 0700, the
  # path the API's image makes (the README, Quarantine and Backups).
  media-quarantine:
  # Caddy's state, owned by its own user; the earlier root-owned caddydata and caddyconfig volumes can go.
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  # ntfy's message cache and its auth database (3f). The cache is how a phone gets an alert published while its
  # connection was down; the auth database is rebuilt from infra/ntfy/server.yml at every start.
  ntfy-data:
```

### Replace `packages/contracts/src/media.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

/** Every code the media endpoints add to ErrorEnvelope.error.code (plus the shared ones: invalid_request, not_found, rate_limited). */
export const MediaErrorCode = z.enum(["unsupported_media_type", "file_too_large", "too_many_pending_uploads", "uploads_unavailable", "media_unavailable"]);
export type MediaErrorCode = z.infer<typeof MediaErrorCode>;

/** Why processing an upload failed. Reported on the status response, not as an HTTP error. */
export const MediaFailure = z.enum(["unsupported_format", "animated_not_supported", "image_too_large", "corrupt_image", "processing_failed"]);
export type MediaFailure = z.infer<typeof MediaFailure>;

/** 20 MiB. The API counts bytes while it streams an upload to disk and stops here. */
export const MEDIA_MAX_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024;
export const MEDIA_MAX_PER_POST = 4;
/** The types an upload may declare. The bytes decide; the declaration is checked and then forgotten. */
export const MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES = ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp", "image/avif", "image/gif"] as const;
export type MediaAcceptedType = (typeof MEDIA_ACCEPTED_TYPES)[number];
export const ALT_MAX_LENGTH = 1000;

/** A media id in its canonical lowercase form, which is also how it names files on the media volumes. */
export const MediaId = z.uuid().transform((id) => id.toLowerCase());

export const MEDIA_SIZES = ["small", "large"] as const;
export type MediaSize = (typeof MEDIA_SIZES)[number];

/** Where an image file is served. Views carry these paths, so the server can move images without a client change. */
export function mediaPath(id: string, size: MediaSize): string {
  return `/api/media/${id}/${size}.webp`;
}

/** Length in code points, which is what Postgres char_length counts. */
export function altLength(alt: string): number {
  return Array.from(alt).length;
}

/** Unicode NFC, every run of whitespace (line breaks included) to one space, trimmed. The server and the composer use the same rule. */
export function normalizeAltText(raw: string): string {
  return raw.normalize("NFC").replace(/\s+/gu, " ").trim();
}

const CONTROL = /\p{Cc}/u;

/** An image description as stored: normalized, 1 to 1000 code points, no control characters. */
export const AltText = z
  .string()
  .max(4000)
  .transform(normalizeAltText)
  .refine((alt) => !CONTROL.test(alt), { message: "control characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((alt) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(alt), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
  .refine((alt) => altLength(alt) >= 1, { message: "every image needs a description" })
  .refine((alt) => altLength(alt) <= ALT_MAX_LENGTH, { message: `descriptions have at most ${ALT_MAX_LENGTH} characters` });

/** One image of a new post: an upload that is ready, and its description. */
export const MediaAttachment = z.object({ id: MediaId, alt: AltText });
export type MediaAttachment = z.infer<typeof MediaAttachment>;

export const UploadResponse = z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("processing") });
export type UploadResponse = z.infer<typeof UploadResponse>;

/**
 * The state of one upload, for its owner. Width and height are those of the large size, after rotation. A ready image
 * carries its blurhash, except one that moderation sealed: it is shown to nobody, and the blurhash is made from the image.
 * 3d (design, sections 7.1, 9.6 and 10.2): a ready image on a post whose seal was lifted and whose files are not back in
 * the image store yet says `restoring`, and one whose files korbat recorded as lost says `lost`; at most one of the two.
 */
export const MediaStatusResponse = z
  .discriminatedUnion("status", [
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("processing") }),
    z.object({
      id: MediaId,
      status: z.literal("ready"),
      width: z.number().int().positive(),
      height: z.number().int().positive(),
      blurhash: z.string().min(6).optional(),
      restoring: z.literal(true).optional(),
      lost: z.literal(true).optional(),
    }),
    z.object({ id: MediaId, status: z.literal("failed"), error: MediaFailure }),
  ])
  .refine((answer) => !(answer.status === "ready" && answer.restoring && answer.lost), { message: "an image is either being restored or lost, never both" });
export type MediaStatusResponse = z.infer<typeof MediaStatusResponse>;

/**
 * An image on a post, as a reader who is shown it gets it. `moderation` is set only on the author's own image that
 * moderation withheld or removed, with that state: the author keeps seeing such an image, and nobody else is shown it.
 */
export const MediaView = z.object({
  id: MediaId,
  width: z.number().int().positive(),
  height: z.number().int().positive(),
  blurhash: z.string().min(6),
  alt: z.string(),
  small: z.string(),
  large: z.string(),
  moderation: z.enum(["withheld", "removed"]).optional(),
});
export type MediaView = z.infer<typeof MediaView>;

/**
 * What a reader gets in place of an image they are not shown: its id and the mark, never its size, its blurhash, its
 * description or a path. It is what anyone but the author gets for a withheld or removed image, the same for both states,
 * and what everyone gets for a sealed image, its author included: `sealed` is set only then, and only for the author.
 */
export const HiddenMedia = z.strictObject({ id: MediaId, hidden: z.literal(true), sealed: z.literal(true).optional() });
export type HiddenMedia = z.infer<typeof HiddenMedia>;

/** Whether an entry of a post's media list is a hidden image, which has nothing to draw or to open. */
export function isHiddenMedia(item: MediaView | HiddenMedia): item is HiddenMedia {
  return "hidden" in item;
}
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { Email, OpaqueId, TurnstileToken } from "./auth";
import { hex, sha256, sha256Bytes, sortedJson, utf8 } from "./canonical";
import { MediaId } from "./media";
import { ALERT_CHANNEL_STATES, GAP_CLASSES, GAP_DISPOSITIONS, ORDER_RULES, OrderNoticeFacts, OrderTexts, OrdersUnverified, ReportsOwed, type OrderGround } from "./orders";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

// Moderation cases (3c design, section 10): the constants and digests that the database, the API, the console, the app,
// the mails and the terms share. Each is the one source its words and numbers are taken from. This module imports
// nothing from staff.ts, and the index evaluates it first, so staff.ts can read these constants while it loads; an import
// the other way round would be a cycle that fails at load. For the same reason it imports nothing from social.ts, whose
// shapes may come to name this module's constants: what a notice needs of a post's id and of a handle is written here.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- rules, categories and keywords

/** The rulebook's rule ids. @korbat/rules holds the rules themselves; the contracts never import it. */
export const RULE_IDS = ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"] as const;
export type RuleId = (typeof RULE_IDS)[number];

/**
 * The 16 categories of the Commission's Transparency Database (read 2026-10-02), which every intake and decision carries.
 * The migration's CHECK lists are written from this constant, and a database test holds them to it. A value the
 * Commission removes stays here: a kept row may hold it, and only the lists offered for new input drop it.
 */
export const TDB_CATEGORIES = [
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
] as const;
export type TdbCategory = (typeof TDB_CATEGORIES)[number];

/** The two categories a notifier never chooses: a rule-only report gets the first, a notifier who is not sure the second. */
type UnofferedCategory = "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" | "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE";
export type TdbFormCategory = Exclude<TdbCategory, UnofferedCategory>;

/** The 14 categories the illegal-ground form shows. */
export const TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES: readonly TdbFormCategory[] = TDB_CATEGORIES.filter(
  (category): category is TdbFormCategory => category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" && category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
);

/**
 * The four choices of the path for child sexual abuse material and the Transparency Database keyword each stores. "abuse"
 * stores none: the database has no keyword for it.
 */
export const CSAM_KEYWORDS = {
  csam: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL",
  deepfake: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE",
  grooming: "KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS",
  abuse: null,
} as const;
export type CsamKeywordChoice = keyof typeof CSAM_KEYWORDS;

/** The keywords a decision on the law may carry: in 3c only the Transparency Database's "Terrorist content". */
export const DECISION_KEYWORDS = ["KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT"] as const;
export type DecisionKeyword = (typeof DECISION_KEYWORDS)[number];

/** The category the composer presets for a decision under each rule. */
export const RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY = {
  R1: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  R2: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  R3: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  R4: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  R5: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
  R6: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
} as const satisfies Record<RuleId, TdbCategory>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- lanes

/** The queue's lanes: 0 is the most urgent. A case takes the most severe lane of its unanswered items. */
export type Lane = 0 | 1 | 2;

/** R2 and R5 are urgent; R3 and R4 come next; R1 and R6 last. */
const RULE_LANES: Record<RuleId, Lane> = { R1: 2, R2: 0, R3: 1, R4: 1, R5: 0, R6: 2 };

/** The categories that are not in lane 2: violence, public security and self-harm are urgent; six more come next. */
```
